The computational contribution is therefore a change in which original contin-
uation values are purchased and how their errors enter a decision, rather than an
internal fit-score improvement. A geometric precision schedule can stop at the first
qualified resolution, while a complete fallback handles an intrinsically inadequate
candidate or supporting minorant. The retained completed-incumbent rule gives
strict original-policy improvement. Its remaining-gain budget bounds the economic
improvement sacrificed by stopping further search. A coupled supplementary ac-
count integrates common-density policy comparisons, atom-safe tail remainders
and signed recursive gain transport, with the independently frozen earlier research
on that question credited in the development companion.
The numerical study holds the original two-date investment technology, continu-
ous innovation distribution, nested AVaR preference, feasible actions, terminal con-
troller and accuracy targets fixed. Eight arms share fresh paid terminal-value labels:
the online semi-analytic Bellman control, a rank-six quadratic, ReLU, its equivalent
conventional hinge, coordinate splines, full quadratic and cubic polynomials, and
tensor-grid interpolation. Each arm receives the same candidate policies under
each contemporaneous certificate service. Three separately frozen phases retain
32,256 primary decisions and 50,176 fresh-process timing decisions, together with
acquisition, fitting audits, rejected attempts, repairs, original-law reference calcula-
tions and failures. Phase A establishes the active-tail implementation; its adverse
elapsed-work comparison motivates phase B’s bounded preliminary acquisition.
Phase B’s remaining overhead motivates phase C’s packed original evaluation. The
latter two phases are explicit development on the previously observed catalogue.
Every control is executed afresh, and neither phase replaces the observations of its
predecessor.
Phase C’s packed service is faster than its uncombined budgeted control in all
16 median-clock cells and faster than the retained geometric service in ten, with all
six losses reported. The ReLU service-time ratios against the geometric control are
0.8614 and 0.8494 at the two risk levels. Returned policies are unchanged across
services, so their economic cost contrasts are exactly zero. With fresh standalone ac-
quisition and actual model loading charged, the quadratic control still has the lower
original mean economic cost and lower complete component cost at both risk levels.

The contribution builds on established risk-averse dynamic programming and
policy iteration (Ruszczy´nski, 2010, 2014), the AVaR variational formulation (Rock-
afellar and Uryasev, 2002), and information-based integration (Novak, 2015).
Inexact-oracle optimization and decision-focused learning clarify related accuracy
and acquisition questions (Devolder et al., 2014, Elmachtoub and Grigas, 2022). Here
the mathematical addition is the joint tail-location and integration account with
matching tail-length dependence, and its outward implementation as an all-action
certificate under the same original economic law. The compiler and these certificates
are available to every representation. Formula information and derivative access
are charged and distinguished from exact point values.
The original NBO program also concerns stochastic control and nonlinear recur-
sive utility. A Brownian Markov BSDE verification theorem states an admissible
connection, including driver measurability, the critic graph z = σT∇u, actor-chain
derivatives, terminal data and stopping-boundary errors. General NDU/FBSDE
systems require their own existence, information and objective assumptions. The
investment evidence is attached to its nested AVaR objective, while the recursive-
utility theorem is attached to the utility problem it actually proves.
The complete article retains earlier original-policy improvements and their eco-
nomic stopping costs, the historical quadratic complete-work winner, all 36 im-
proved residual spans accompanied by an increase from 644 to 757 first-proposal
rejections, and the unestablished neural-adoption regions. These observations moti-
vate action-aware acquisition and stronger numerical methods. Current progress
is evaluated by new proofs, complete decisions and paid work. Neural-specific
representation advantages, prospective acquisition validation, longer horizons and
calibrated economic adoption remain distinct research obligations. The supple-
ment supplies complete mathematical arguments; the development companion
and source archive preserve earlier theories, applications, adverse evidence and
independently frozen experiments.

APPENDIX AM: TAIL-AWARE ACTION ACCURACY
A critic can match action derivatives pointwise in the innovation and still propose
the wrong risk-averse action. The missing quantity is the change in the adverse tail.
This section refines the directional account in Theorem A.1; it does not replace an
original-law witness by a training statistic.
Fix a state and a realized action a. On the same original probability space let Za
be the true continuation outcome and Ha an acquired surrogate. In a neighborhood
of a, suppose both are almost surely differentiable with integrably dominated
derivatives. At a assume their α-quantiles are unique, carry no mass, and cut off
upper tails of probability t = 1 −α, where 0 < α < 1. These are local assumptions,
not automatic properties of every fitted ReLU. Choose a constant c and certified
numbers ϵ, δ ≥0 such that
∥Za −Ha −c∥∞≤ϵ,
∥∇aZa −∇aHa∥∞≤δ.
The constant is an anchor-level centering; no derivative of a data-dependent cen-
tering rule is taken. Write η for the true quantile, Bϵ = {|Za −η| ≤2ϵ}, and, for an
arbitrary vector v0,
Gϵ = esssup

The proof localizes changed tail membership to a quantile band and uses the zero
total mass of the difference between two maximizing densities. Thus a constant
component of the surrogate action gradient cancels: tail gradient oscillation, rather
than its overall magnitude, controls the switching cost. Under a positive margin
exponent, joint control of the centered value error and directional error gives a
rate for action loss. A finite validation sample does not itself verify C, κ or the
essential suprema. At atoms or nonunique tails the stated differentiability theorem
is unavailable; the feasible-density minorants of Theorem A.1 remain the appro-
priate certification device. When Za uses an optimal continuation, (A.43) bounds
the current-action gap; an imperfect implemented future policy requires its sepa-
rate recursive allowance before interpreting the bound as complete-policy regret.
Numerical witness slack is paid there through U −L, not silently dropped from
(A.43).
An exact diagnostic.
Let z be uniform on [−1,1], α = 1/2, a ∈[−1,1], and stage
cost a2. Take Za = (a + 1)z and Ha = (a −1)z. Their action derivatives are identi-
cally z, yet the original and surrogate optimal actions are −1/4 and 1/4. Using the
surrogate action incurs original loss 1/4. This continuous-law diagnostic, indepen-
dently integrated in rational arithmetic, rules out any general action-loss bound
that vanishes with directional error alone. It is not the investment economy, a new
population sample, or an empirical neural advantage. Its conceptual provenance in
the earlier tail-aware research protocols is retained.
Acquisition target and novelty.
For a family satisfying verified margin assump-
tions, a useful acquisition target is the bound in (A.43), with envelope slack and
actual qualification work added. The earlier prospective finite-menu selection theo-
rem then applies to complete services with that verified certificate. Our executed
comparison below does not retroactively become a training experiment for this
new loss: its frozen acquisition remains least squares. CVaR gradient estimation
and decision-focused learning already have established formulations (Tamar et al.,
2015, Luo and Delage, 2026, Elmachtoub and Grigas, 2022). The present result is a
centered, tail-localized perturbation bound tied to the same constrained Bellman
action and a valid complete-policy account. The static trajectory-CVaR objective of

AM.1. A bounded preliminary information budget
Resolving fewer innovation locations need not reduce complete decision work.
Tail localization, several refused resolutions, and eventual repair can outweigh
the saved quadrature. We therefore introduce a second service whose preliminary
work is bounded before the original complete solver is invoked. Phase B freezes
this algorithm after the retained Phase A outcomes; its acquisition, conventional
controls, reference intervals, and timing processes constitute a separate experiment.
Fix the original state, a feasible realized actor proposal, the original risk level
α ∈{1/2,3/4}, and the implemented terminal policy. Two floating endpoint com-
parisons propose a boundary cut when possible. Only the remaining rows receive
six floating bisection steps. These signs have no certification authority: the resulting
feasible cut is rounded to the declared dyadic grid, and two outward original-
continuation values construct the defect κ in (A.14). This defect is retained at every
resolution. The service omits exactly zero-length tails, attempts two and then four
equal cells per positive-length tail, and accepts only a certificate meeting both origi-
nal targets. Otherwise it invokes the frozen 128-bin complete service from the same
already acquired proposal, including its original repair, refinement, and rational
fallback.
PROPOSITION A.16—Original-policy qualification with bounded preliminary
work: Under the outward-oracle and original-policy assumptions of Theorem A.3, the
stated service returns only certificates valid for the original investment objective. Its prelim-
inary work uses at most
Noutward ≤30,
Nfloating ≤16

complete service. An outward payload includes the original value enclosure and the valid
supporting information required by the action certificate. Calls repeated at the same location
are counted again.

More precisely, if the selected density has p ∈{1,2} nonempty tails, the outward bound
is 2 + 14p; an acceptance at the first resolution uses at most 2 + 5p. A floating endpoint
exit uses only four floating values. The two outward defect values are acquired once and
shared across the preliminary resolutions. If the underlying oracle calls and frozen complete
service terminate, adding this finite prelude preserves that termination and the original loss
and width targets.
These are bounds on added terminal information, not on elapsed time or on
the complete internal work of a terminal solve. Actor acquisition, the payloads’
numerical construction, rejected attempts, density and certificate algebra, and the
complete invoked fallback remain paid work. Early acceptance can avoid a conven-
tional repair and can therefore change the returned action. Its original economic cost
must be compared using its own reference interval; no zero-cost or improvement
conclusion follows from the point-count bound.
The masked-tail ablation applies the same exact zero-mass omission and floating
proposal rule while retaining all six resolutions 2,4,8,16,32,64. It separates the
effect of removing zero-mass work from the additional decision to cap preliminary
effort. Every representation, including the conventional hinge encoding of ReLU,
receives the same service and information access.
AM.2. From the payload budget to original decision work
A bound on purchased point values does not by itself bound elapsed decision
work. The original compiler has a fixed cost for array construction, outward opera-
tions and its certified terminal controller. Calling it separately for each nonempty tail
component can therefore lose time even when it acquires fewer original values. We
implement Proposition A.16’s two-resolution prelude by packing its positive-weight
midpoint and endpoint requests into one original compiler call per attempted reso-
lution.
Each packed entry carries its original state, action, innovation and request type.
The inverse indices return its lower value, upper value and supporting slope to
the original selected-tail summand. A singleton innovation axis prevents a cross-
product between different entries. Repeated locations remain separate paid requests;

APPENDIX AN: POLICY IMPROVEMENT, STOPPING AND THE LEARNING GRAPH
The certificate separates three choices: which continuation to acquire, which
feasible action to propose, and whether to spend more work on that action. The
first two determine a candidate complete policy. A tighter enclosure of that same
policy changes the information available for the third choice. Actual improvement
requires a comparison of original policy values.
Completed policies and foregone gain.
Let a completed feasible incumbent have
a verified cost bracket [LB,UB] and let OB be a valid lower bound on the original
optimum. A completed trial with upper cost UT < LB delivers a strict original-
policy improvement, provided it also meets the unchanged qualification targets.
The improvement is at least LB −UT. The remaining possible gain from any further
feasible policy is at most
GB = max{0,UB −OB}.
Thus stopping when GB ≤η has an explicit original-objective opportunity cost. For
a monetary value v per unit of original loss and a lower bound c on an additional
computation’s cost, c ≥vGB rules out a strictly positive net gain from that com-
putation. The converse inequality does not guarantee that a useful improvement
will be found. The complete original theorems, interface sharpness and recursive
risk-distorted composition are retained in Development Sections BA and BB, with
full proofs in the supplement. Their R110 experiments retain their own actual policy
gains and positive foregone gains; they are not new R119 observations.
An action comparison can share a risk witness.
For bounded original continuations
X,Y and one common feasible dual law q, write kX(q) = ρ(X) −{EqX −ψ(q)} ≥0.

Supplement Theorem A.4 proves a computable action contrast using the two
original-risk defects, with an atom-safe quantile-band remainder. Its implemented-
future allowance is charged once on each side of the contrast. Proposition A.5
proves that a continuation contrast of oscillation w > 0 only needs dual laws whose
reference optimality slack is at most w, without assuming the supremum is attained.
This preserves the signed recursive policy difference instead of discarding the refer-
ence slack. The integral of a difference of convex continuations still needs a valid
separate enclosure. This mathematical interface advances the independently frozen
R111–R112 question; no current numerical result is attributed to a paired algorithm
that has not been implemented.
The actor and critic are a specified computational graph.
For a smooth critic uθ and a
differentiable feasible actor aω, the Bellman residual includes the derivative through
the actor and through every parameter-dependent continuation and transition.
Differentiating the half-squared residual gives E[rθ,ω∇rθ,ω] under the integrability
and differentiation hypotheses in Supplement Section 10. Holding a target fixed
defines a different update and requires its own convergence argument. Discrete
original-law qualification treats a realized rounded action as a feasible decision and
does not differentiate its numerical rounding operation.
For the Brownian Markov recursive-utility interface, the critic graph is zu = σT∇u.
The driver, admissible controls, terminal condition and stopping boundary belong
to that same recursive criterion. Supplement Proposition S.12 proves the stopped-
domain residual account, including its stability factor and boundary discrepancy. A
general ReLU critic is not a classical C1,2 Itô test function merely because its ordinary
Hessian vanishes away from kinks. The discrete NBO construction remains valid
under its own hypotheses. Fully coupled NDU/FBSDE systems and other utility
objectives require their own well-posedness and verification premises; they do not
inherit the investment experiment’s numerical ranking by a change of terminology.

APPENDIX AO: ORIGINAL INVESTMENT DECISIONS: INFORMATION AND

AO.1. The economic comparison and its information budget
We evaluate whether resolving the active innovation tails reduces the cost of a
certified original Bellman decision. The economic model remains (13)–(14): two
investment dates, a nonlinear transition, the original state-dependent investment
capacity, discount 15/16, a continuous uniform innovation on [−1/32,1/32], and
nested upper-cost AVaR at α = 1/2 and 3/4. The actual last-date controller, its
observation rule, and its 2−20 uniform continuation allowance are unchanged. At the
first date every completed service must certify regret at most 1/256 and an original-
policy cost interval of width at most 1/8192. Theorem A.3 establishes why these
criteria concern the original economic objective, including the implemented future
decisions. Numerical integration encloses the original continuous law throughout.
The intervention holds each acquired continuation representation and its realized
first-date proposal fixed while changing the information used for qualification.
The eight arms are the online semi-analytic Bellman control, quadratic, ReLU, its
equivalent conventional hinge, coordinate spline, degree-two and degree-three
polynomials, and grid interpolation. The rank-six quadratic, ReLU and spline con-
structions retain their common 32-feature dictionaries, three nonlinear selections,
nonnegative nonlinear coefficients, tie rule and 30-bit rounding. The broader poly-
nomial and grid baselines retain their additional representational flexibility and
reported memory requirements. The hinge receives exactly the acquired ReLU
coefficients and its full standalone acquisition charge. It provides a conventional
implementation of the same information and feasible policies.
In each phase we newly acquire the 256 original-model terminal-value labels on
the fixed 16 × 16 grid for each risk level. Every competing fit receives the same label
bytes. Acquisition includes all candidates, exclusions, independent feature-matrix
and active-face QR audits, serialization and reloading. The primary catalogue is all
144 states of the fixed 12 × 12 grid. These are deterministic numerical catalogues;
no population confidence interval or unseen-sample claim attaches to them. The
experiment concerns the acquired last-continuation slice of NBO in this original

was slower than both controls at both risk levels in every recorded repeat. The full
48-row frontier, including these losses, remains in the development companion.

AO.4. Information theory and the scope of scaling evidence
The separate exact point-information catalogue tests Theorem A.2 on ten pre-
declared convex piecewise-linear/quadratic functions, eight risk levels from zero
through 255/256, and four resolutions. All 320 cells and 2,901 rational checks are
retained. The active-tail interval is narrower in 242 cells, whole-support quadrature
is narrower in 27, and 51 tie. Both methods obey the same declared query cap;
actual distinct queries are reported separately. At α = 0, whole-support wins 20
of 40 cells and active integration wins eight. Nearer the upper risk limit active
localization uses the shorter adverse support, consistently with the theorem’s 1 −α
factor. Exact independent integrals and cut reconstruction are evaluation evidence;
formula access is not provided to either point-query algorithm.
Phase A also compares the same original online proposal with a compiled 128-bin
certificate and an eight-cell-per-tail certificate at dimensions 2,4,8. All 192 paired
contexts qualify. The active/compiled certificate time ratios are approximately
0.515,0.475, 0.423,0.424, and 0.391,0.317 across the two risks. Charging their com-
mon proposal moves the ratios to 0.829,0.793, 0.757,0.763, and 0.690,0.659. These
are original-model primitive scaling observations. They do not establish a com-
plete learned high-dimensional service, a multivariate risk integration theorem, or
a longer-horizon convergence rate. The mathematical information improvement,
its action-valid certificate, and these implementation limitations together specify
the next economic computational problem; all historical adverse and incomplete
episodes remain attributable in the development companion.

AO.5. Packed original-law evaluation: a separately frozen implementation
The negative masking result motivates a further implementation experiment,
phase C, prospectively committed at 095936f1 after the outcomes of phases A and
B were known. It repeats all five controls, acquisition, reference calculations and
seven timing processes afresh. The sixth service, fused tail (F), purchases exactly the
positive-mass midpoint and endpoint payloads required by the two-level budget,
in one packed call to the unchanged original terminal compiler at each resolution.
It then scatters the returned values and slopes to their original state/action identi-
ties and performs the same outward aggregation. No duplicate requested payload
is made free. The density, certified cut defect, 2−20 implemented-continuation al-
lowance, original action interval, qualification targets and complete fallback remain
unchanged. This is post-A/B development on the previously observed catalogue,
not an unseen validation or a retrospective alteration of either earlier experiment.
All 13,824 primary and 21,504 timing decisions completed. The native exact

APPENDIX AP: CONCLUSION
Neural Bellman Operators link recursively acquired continuations to feasible
original-objective decisions. The complete account includes the actor’s own future
policy, action-dependent continuation error, original-law numerical witnesses and
the cost of obtaining them. The original construction and the completed-policy safe-
guards establish precise decision guarantees without assuming that an optimizer
successfully trains an arbitrary network.

The present revision identifies the adverse innovation region as a paid informa-
tion decision. For scalar uniform risk and convex Lipschitz continuations, locating
that region before integration yields matching deterministic bounds with linear
tail-length dependence. The original investment primitives turn an approximate
location into an outward all-action certificate, and a finite preliminary budget limits
work spent before the complete original solver is invoked. These contributions
concern the information and certification components of NBOs and are available to
all same-information representations.
The experiments distinguish information savings, service time and economic
loss. They retain every fixed-catalogue decision, every timing repetition, all rejected
certificates, independently paid references and the strong conventional frontier.
Equivalent ReLU and hinge actors receive equal information and full acquisition
charges. An unchanged complete policy has unchanged original economic value.
Computational adoption therefore requires both a competitive complete service
and a justified economic workload; a smaller fitting residual or a smaller query
count alone does not establish it.
The research program continues toward prospective action-aware acquisition,
neural-specific benefits under matched resources, larger dynamic economic prob-
lems and calibrated use. The new proofs and executed algorithms make those
questions more sharply testable. The complete supplement states the mathemati-
cal assumptions and proofs, while the development companion retains the earlier
applications, policy improvements, negative experiments, unresolved claims and
independent source identities needed to continue that program.

AR.2. Boundary data and viscosity selection
Zero interior residual does not choose terminal or lateral data: with zero flow
and dynamics, every constant has zero interior residual, while terminal payoff
zero selects only the zero constant. Proposition S.10 specifies the terminal function,
admissibility, continuous Bellman class, measurability, and policy recursion actually
used in the current finite-horizon model. Proposition S.12 specifies the separate
Brownian boundary/terminal discrepancy under stopping. An infinite-horizon
claim additionally requires the stated function class and contraction or transversality
hypotheses; it does not follow from a finite-horizon argument.
Even exact boundary data and vanishing population squared residual do not give
a general viscosity-selection theorem. For the deterministic exit problem with speed
in [−1,1] and payoff minus elapsed time, the equation is 1 −|V′| = 0 on (−1,1)
with zero boundary values. Its value is V∗(x) = |x| −1. The smooth functions

subsolution inequality. The displayed integral follows by expanding the square on

are explicit inputs to the current certificates. A theorem on approximating a smooth
target and its derivatives does not approximate nonexistent classical derivatives
at a kink, prove optimization of a fixed architecture, or provide a PDE comparison
principle.

AR.4. The expected stochastic-Hessian objective
If bq is conditionally unbiased for the diffusion trace q, then
E[(a −bq/2)2 | a, q] = (a −q/2)2 + 1
4 Var(bq | a, q).
The conditioning here fixes the network, state, and all non-probe quantities. The
variance usually depends on the network derivatives. For one standard Gaus-
sian probe with bq = hZ2 and a = 1, Gaussian second and fourth moments give
1 −h + 3h2/4, minimized at h = 2/3, whereas the true square is minimized at
h = 2. Two conditionally independent probe banks give the unbiased product
E[(a −bq1/2)(a −bq2/2)] = (a −q/2)2. The individual product can be negative and
its variance remains a numerical cost. For covariance σσ⊤, a symmetric matrix
actually probed is σ⊤D2Vσ; for a nonsymmetric representation, the quadratic form
uses its symmetric part. Unbiasedness of an unweighted trace does not validate
a diffusion-weighted implementation or a squared loss. No current theorem con-
cludes feasibility failure from trace noise when the executed actor is hard-mapped
into the feasible box.

al-methods-r15/section-14/embedded-6.
Request. R15 also retains an evidentiary classification issue. The dimension-10 HJB superi-
ority claim is not a fully prospectively frozen result. The original interval crossed zero; after
inspecting the original transfer width, the author developed a sharper deterministic transfer
theorem and applied it to the same observations. If that theorem is correct and uniform, using
it need not invalidate coverage. The manuscript discloses the sequence and preserves the
original interval. But the resulting dimension-10 sign should be described as a transparent
post-freeze analytical reanalysis and independently replicated with the refined transfer fixed
in advance, not presented on the same footing as the original dimension-50 confirmation.
Author action. The dimension-10 HJB sign remains a post-freeze analytical reanalysis of
the original observations, distinct from the original dimension-50 confirmation. R119 A/B/
C use the same disclosure principle: later frozen development does not become an unseen
confirmatory study.
Remaining requirement. No current scalar investment evaluation supplies the separately
requested independent HJB replication.

algorithm.

Author action. The inherited centered-risk proof retains nonnegative penalty with infimum

3.1 Deterministic AVaR information lower bound, paragraph 2
Exact item identifier. 2026-10-1
4-econometrica-numerical-methods-r97/section-45/embedded-2.
Request. The result must nevertheless be stated narrowly. It is a deterministic, univariate,
point-value oracle lower bound for a uniform law and a fixed AVaR level. It does not cover
randomized algorithms, derivative or formula access, nonuniform laws, multiple innovations,
or a continuation supplied in a representation that can be integrated analytically. The lower
and upper constants also have opposite dependence on ‘1-alpha‘; the theorem matches the
exponent at fixed ‘alpha‘, not a tail-uniform constant.

convex-Lipschitz uniform-law assumptions and explicitly charges localization. It strengthens
the historical fixed-alpha constant mismatch to a common linear tail factor for N at least 32.
Remaining requirement. Bit complexity, derivative/formula oracles, randomized and
multivariate-risk information require separate results.

AU.4. Every preliminary payload and unresolved scientific claim

including timing rows. The complete masked ladder has 2,304 primary rows and
3,584 timing rows. Its primary resolution histories are 1,098 rows at level 2, 962
at levels 2 and 4, and 244 exhausting all six levels; these consume 94,925 outward
payloads. The budgeted service has the same 1,098 level-2 exits and 1,206 two-level
histories, consuming 28,801 outward payloads and entering complete fallback at
precisely the 244 exhausted rows. The corresponding timing payload totals are

experimental identities. None of the present observations completes their missing

APPENDIX AX: RETAINED R110 INTRODUCTION AND ECONOMIC FRAMING
APPENDIX AY: INTRODUCTION
Dynamic investment under risk requires a continuation value, a feasible action
and a decision about how much computation to purchase. These objects cannot be
assessed independently. A more accurately fitted continuation can move a nearly
binding action in the wrong direction; a better proposed action can still require an
expensive original-model certificate; and a certified policy improvement can be too
small to justify another round of computation. Neural Bellman Operators (NBOs)
study this joint problem by constructing continuation and policy maps, evaluating
their own future decisions, and qualifying their loss under the original economic
law.
The economic question is when an acquired neural continuation helps deliver
original-objective decisions at a competitive complete cost. The comparison is
with conventional representations given the same information, feasible actions and
computational components. A theorem whose validity is representation neutral is
not evidence that neural networks alone can implement it. Equally, a negative result
for one fitting loss does not exhaust what an action-aligned continuation and policy
construction can achieve.
We develop an original-law chain from continuation accuracy to feasible deci-
sions and paid stopping. The retained own-future NBO construction returns an
exactly realizable neural continuation and a measurable feasible actor without as-
suming successful nonconvex training. Reference-centered recursive-risk bounds
distinguish action-dependent errors from irrelevant level shifts. An original-law
supporting quadratic then bounds the gap of the action actually proposed, includ-
ing constrained stationarity and numerical witness slack. All these accounts refer to
the original Bellman operator, not to an easier fitted economy.
Nonlinear risk creates an additional obstruction. Two continuation outcomes
can have identical action derivatives at every innovation and still have different

risk-optimal actions because their maximizing tails differ. A centered quantile-
band theorem bounds this discrepancy using value error, directional error and the
oscillation of the action gradient near the tail boundary. Its exact continuous-law
diagnostic has zero directional approximation error but original action loss 1/4. The
conditions under which the bound is differentiable, the treatment of boundaries
and the separate allowance for an imperfect implemented future policy are explicit.
A finite training sample is not a certificate of its uniform margin assumptions.
The second contribution concerns the economic return to further computation. We
first derive an active-region terminal Bellman oracle from the original investment
primitives. Its action derivative is a strictly increasing cubic on at most four regions.
Formula-derived actions are independently qualified by the original outward wit-
ness; numerical inversion never acquires certificate authority. This provides a strong
semi-analytic control to every representation. We then retain a completed qualified
incumbent and accept a new action only when its policy-cost upper bound lies
strictly below the incumbent’s lower bound. A recursive gain theorem states when
such local inequalities support a uniform policy-improvement conclusion.
The current algorithmic addition uses the same original-optimum lower bound
to cap remaining policy improvement. When that cap is below a predeclared gain
budget, a state stops paying for further support and trial evaluations. Qualifica-
tion targets remain unchanged. We prove the pointwise foregone-gain guaran-
tee, its finite-catalogue account, and its recursive composition under the required
comparator-future residual. The stopping rule does not pretend to be globally op-
timal metareasoning, nor does it assign an invented price to economic welfare. It
makes an implementable, testable trade-off between actual original-policy cost and
complete computational work.
The numerical comparison preserves the original two-date continuous-risk in-
vestment economy. Eight proposal arms share 256 paid terminal-value labels: an
online original-model service, rank-six quadratic, ReLU and coordinate-spline con-
tinuations, an equivalent conventional hinge, full quadratic and cubic polynomials,
and bilinear tensor interpolation. An unchanged-source reproduction retains all
4,096 decisions in the original four-service comparison. The new experiment re-
tains all 6,144 decisions in six services, including the original controls, the primary

The evidence improves the computation–decision connection without manufac-
turing a neural victory. At the primary budget, the new rule omits 2,386 of 3,072
possible extra support/trial pairs across the declared arms and risks. For ReLU
at risk level 1/2, original terminal-risk queries fall from 94,737 to 35,832, and the
median complete 32-state service clock falls from about 0.4074 to 0.2074 seconds.
Its mean original cost rises relative to the full safeguard by a certified interval
contained in [1.95,3.34] × 10−7; that foregone improvement is reported, not hidden
as equal accuracy. The budgeted service still strictly improves its completed plain
incumbent. Conventional methods receive the same stopping benefit, and ReLU
and equivalent hinges return exactly identical policy and trial records.
Relation to established methods and evidence.
Risk-averse dynamic programming
and policy iteration already provide the recursive foundation (Ruszczy´nski, 2010,
2014). Inexact-oracle optimization separates computation from its accuracy account
(Devolder et al., 2014); decision-focused learning and CVaR differentiation provide
related acquisition and gradient principles (Elmachtoub and Grigas, 2022, Tamar
et al., 2015). Our results specify their connection to original-law supporting wit-
nesses, tail switching, completed feasible policies, risk-distorted gains and charged
resolution. The retained information bounds have explicit oracle restrictions; a
formula-derived compiler is not a counterexample to a point-value lower bound.
Recent static trajectory-CVaR work (Luo and Delage, 2026) optimizes a different
recursive object from the nested AVaR preference here. Its numerical improvements
cannot be transferred between those objectives.
The original NBO identity includes rigorous connections to recursive utility and
stochastic control. A self-contained Brownian Markov BSDE verification result in
the supplement states one admissible bridge, including well-posedness, the critic
computational graph and terminal or stopping-boundary errors. It does not assume

APPENDIX BA: SAFEGUARDED POLICY IMPROVEMENT AND RESOLUTION
Qualification and improvement answer different questions. A completed policy
may satisfy a loss tolerance without minimizing cost, and a rejected early proposal
is not the completed conventional baseline. We retain a qualified incumbent before
attempting any improvement.
PROPOSITION A.17—Completed-incumbent improvement: Fix the original state,
law, feasible action set and complete future policy. Suppose two feasible current actions
have verified complete-policy cost intervals [l, u] and [l′, u′]. Replacing the incumbent only
when u′ < l guarantees a strict cost decrease of at least l −u′ > 0. Repeating this rule
preserves weak improvement relative to the initial completed incumbent. Requiring every
replacement also to pass the original-optimum and policy-width targets preserves those
targets. A refused trial leaves the incumbent unchanged but still incurs its full work.
This rule is an interval implementation of a descent safeguard, not a new claim
that descent is uniquely neural. In the executed service, three projected support steps
are attempted, with fractions 1,1/2,1/4, after the original fallback and refinement
have completed. An original-optimum lower bound can be reused across actions at

BA.2. Paid precision and a stopping rule
A strict descent gate can be undecided because two policy intervals overlap.
Suppose a fixed incumbent and candidate have actual improvement ∆= J −J′, and
refinement at resolution n gives intervals containing their respective costs, with
widths at most A/n2 and A′/n2. Then

is an information obstruction: an algorithm cannot certify strict descent for every
pair of costs consistent with two overlapping intervals. Thus the claimed resolution
scale belongs to this interval interface, not a new universal lower bound for all

APPENDIX BB: CERTIFIED REMAINING GAIN AND PAID STOPPING
A completed NBO service should not keep paying for improvements that cannot
be economically material. The relevant stopping quantity is not a critic’s training
residual. It is an upper bound on the remaining improvement in the original decision
problem. We turn that bound into a statewise allocation rule, with an explicit price in
possible foregone policy improvement. The rule is available to every representation;
it is not a neural-specific optimization principle.
BB.1. A certificate interface in units of original cost
Fix a state, the original information and law, and the same implemented future
policy. An incumbent action is already feasible and qualified. Its cost is J, its verified
interval is [l, u], and b ≤V∗is a verified lower bound for the original optimal value.
Let
e = up(u −b),
e ≥0,
where up denotes a genuine outward arithmetic bound, not a favorable rounding
of an optimizer’s return value. Qualification still means the original loss and policy-
width targets. Choose an additional, separately declared improvement budget
θ ≥0.
THEOREM A.19—Remaining-gain stopping and a complete-service comparison:
If e ≤θ, retaining the incumbent and stopping all further improvement at that state
preserves its qualification and, for every feasible original policy ν, gives
(J −Jν)+ ≤e ≤θ.
(A.48)

The competitor may have a better future policy: the lower bound b concerns the original
optimum, not only the fixed-future action optimum.
Consider a finite safeguarded improvement procedure and a shortened version that starts
from the same completed incumbent. The shortened procedure uses the same trial and
acceptance rules until it stops by (A.48); at an un-stopped state suppose its complete trace
agrees with the full procedure. Denote the returned policy costs by Jshort and Jfull. Then
(Jshort(x) −Jfull(x))+ ≤1{stopped at x}estop(x).
(A.49)
For a declared finite catalogue with nonnegative weights wi summing to one, the weighted
mean positive-part loss is at most ∑i: stopped wiestop(xi). For identical returned actions and
the same future policy, the cost contrast is exactly zero, not the width of two independently
subtracted intervals.
From [l, u] and b alone, the ceiling u −b cannot generally be reduced. This is sharpness
of the declared certificate interface, not an information lower bound against a solver given
additional formulas, derivative information or a sharper feasible-policy enclosure.
A final state can have e > θ after using all allowed trials without stopping. It
must still meet the unchanged original qualification target. Thus θ is not a relaxed
or tightened substitute for the original policy-regret tolerance. The trace-agreement
premise also matters in floating arithmetic: batching only the active rows can
alter arithmetic order in an implementation that is not rowwise deterministic. Our
protocol records and checks that issue; a mathematical stopping bound does not
itself establish bitwise equality of all un-stopped computations.
The complete implementation first runs the compiled original-law service to
qualification. It then considers the same three support-step fractions 1,1/2,1/4 as
the full safeguard. Before each round it stops a row when e ≤θ, retaining that row’s
action and certificate. Remaining rows pay for the original-law supporting query
and fresh policy-cost enclosure. A changed action is accepted only by strict interval
separation and both original qualification predicates. The stopping comparisons,
active masks, refused trials and omitted trial slots are all recorded. Neither a cheap
surrogate loss nor a noncertified estimate of improvement authorizes stopping.

BB.2. What propagates through a recursive problem
A root-state guarantee with a fixed future policy is not a uniform multi-date

BE.2. Sound random intervals and randomized point estimates
A randomized algorithm can mean a zero-failure enclosure or a statistical ap-
proximation. We call an interval procedure pathwise sound if, outside one null set
of random tapes independent of the input, it contains the risk of every admissible
input consistent with the tape’s transcript. This is stronger than requiring coverage
1 −δ separately for each input.

APPENDIX BF: A DECISION-THEORETIC VALUE OF ACQUIRED OBLIQUE

An approximation separation matters economically only when it changes an
implemented decision. We give such a realization for the original oblique continua-
tion, without altering the retained investment comparison. This is an exactly solved
economic mechanism, not an empirical calibration or a timing experiment.
A decision maker observes x = (x1, x2) ∈[0,1]2 and a posted price p ∈[0,3].
Purchasing one durable claim yields next-date benefit
v(x) = 1 + (x1 + x2 −1)+.
(A.56)
The feasible action is b ∈{0,1}, and total cost is b{p −v(x)}. This is a two-date
Bellman problem with a deterministic terminal payoff and unit discount. A stored
continuation h(x) ∈[0,3] implements bh(x, p) = 1{p ≤h(x)}. The original optimum
buys at p ≤v(x). A price tie has zero loss. Let states be uniform on the square and
prices uniform on [0,3], independently.

BF.1. Acquisition, conventional geometry and purchase
The mechanism identifies a value of the oblique continuation geometry, not a
value of relabeling its formula as a network. A piecewise-affine conventional rep-
resentation on the two triangles separated by x1 + x2 = 1 is also exact. Convex
regression with that hinge already in its dictionary contains the same exact con-
tinuation. Those controls are included in the exact comparison. Discovering the
separating hyperplane from unknown data, fitting a larger dictionary or construct-
ing an adaptive triangulation are different acquisition problems; their costs cannot
be inferred from this formula-access calculation.

APPENDIX BH: ORIGINAL-POLICY COSTS AND THE PRICE OF REFINEMENT
BH.1. Economic identity, acquisition and prospective design
The experiments use exactly (13)–(14): two dates, two state coordinates, scalar
state-dependent investment capacity, discount 15/16, continuous uniform innova-
tion and nested upper-cost AVaR at α = 1/2 and 3/4. The actual terminal controller
and its 2−20 uniform allowance are unchanged. Every returned policy must have
original-optimum loss at most 1/256 and a policy-cost interval width at most
1/8192. Numerical integration encloses the continuous law rather than replacing it
by a finite-shock economic model.
Every fitted arm receives the same original-model terminal-value enclosures at
the 256 midpoints of a 16 × 16 grid. Their exact production interval midpoints are
regression labels, and their acquisition is charged. The comparison is the acquired
last-continuation slice of NBO; it does not newly train the general own-future
construction at an unreported longer horizon. Evaluation uses all 64 midpoints
of a disjoint 8 × 8 grid. Those catalogues were declared before execution, but the
same design appeared in earlier research protocols. It is not an unseen statistical
sample. The bounds below average the entire declared catalogue and are numerical
intervals, not population confidence intervals. No R96 or R97 statistical interval is
transferred to a newly fitted actor.
Rank-six quadratic, ReLU and coordinate-spline arms use their original 32-feature
dictionaries, three nonlinear selections, nonnegative nonlinear coefficients, the

hinge evaluates precisely the acquired ReLU geometry. Full degree-two and degree-
three polynomials and bilinear interpolation broaden the conventional frontier;
their unequal ranks and memory are recorded, not forced into an artificially weak
neural comparison class. Polynomial and grid action proposals use the fixed scan

The online service illustrates when improvement work is unnecessary: it accepts
no safeguard changes, and the budget rule omits all 192 extra pairs at either risk
level while returning the same policy. Its medians fall from 0.4251 to 0.1486 and
from 0.4451 to 0.1496 seconds in the new matched campaign. Several learned arms
still cost more than that accurate online control after refinement. Quadratic and
spline representations benefit from the same rule; their conventional victories are
not removed. ReLU and equivalent hinges have exactly equal rows and trial records
in all twelve risk-by-service comparisons. Their different clocks are implementation
cost, not a separation of representable policies or acquired information.
The separate unchanged-source reproduction also supports the compiler as a
common original-model improvement. Its online medians decrease from approx-
imately 0.6395 to 0.1380 seconds at 1/2 and from 0.6394 to 0.1514 at 3/4. These
clocks belong to that reproduction, not to the new six-service campaign. Both sets of
seven raw timing repetitions are retained; one is not substituted for the other. The
compiler does not change the deployed terminal controller, and its feasible witness
remains the authority for continuation information.
BH.3. Error budgets, work accounting and adoption
An action-distance bound is reported from original action curvature two and
the verified regret bound. It is not measured error against a freely supplied exact
actor. A separately charged 4,096-bin original-model reference bracket sharpens
the reported regret account; its approximately 10.31 seconds are benchmark work,
not a free deployed-service oracle. A state exhausting all three attempts without
stopping may have regret above θ, but must still satisfy the original 1/256 target.
The stopping budget bounds foregone gain at stopped states; it is never relabeled
the final regret target for every row.
Every acquisition charge includes the common original labels, all feature trials
and exclusions, fitting, independent numerical audit, serialization and reload. Stan-
dalone comparisons charge a fitted service its full share of those costs; the complete
research tournament additionally pays for all competing arms and budgets, refer-
ence work, all audits and all timing processes. The unchanged-source campaign

All clocks are descriptive: seven sequential fresh processes, a fixed within-process
order and one computational thread, with processor frequency and unrelated load
not claimed controlled. We retain every repetition, operation category and cumu-
lative process RSS. Query-event counts are not summed and called floating-point
operations; cumulative process RSS is not an isolated per-arm memory allocation.
The sensitivity appendix reports every declared budget, including larger cost sacri-
fices and smaller work savings. No theta or favorable repetition was selected after
seeing outcomes.
The result is a certified computation–policy trade-off, not a calibrated purchase
decision. A deployment would need an economically justified gain budget, work-
load and compute price, and an acquisition policy chosen without hindsight. The
observed saving does not by itself establish neural adoption over a strong conven-
tional method.
BH.4. Independent checks and retained adverse evidence
The unchanged-source campaign retains 4,096 primary decisions and 14,336
timing decisions; its 18,432 rows and 27,648 safeguard-trial records pass 169,472
independent exact-arithmetic checks. The new campaign retains 6,144 primary
decisions and 21,504 timing decisions; its 27,648 rows and all 69,120 active or
omitted trial slots pass 794,058 checks. The latter includes 32 exact paired inherited-
control identities and all 64 budget comparisons. A separate original-kernel audit
passes 3,072 rational checks over 384 contexts at d = 2,4,8. This is kernel scaling,
not an unexecuted learned high-dimensional or longer-horizon tournament. Sixteen
unchanged-source and twelve new preflight tests also pass. Finite tests support
implementation evidence but do not replace the complete mathematical proofs.
The historical R97 campaign remains distinct: all 36 residual spans decreased, but
total first-proposal rejections increased from 644 to 757. Quadratic rejections rose

absent from the delivered layout. The actual logs are preserved. This is not an
all-green full-history replay, and the successful current campaign cannot repair it by
changing labels. The package separates the current executable dependency closure,
verified outputs and mathematical claims from the outstanding historical archive
dependencies.
APPENDIX BI: CONCLUSION
Neural Bellman Operators concern continuation learning and feasible deci-
sions under the original recursive economic objective. This revision connects
their construction to action-aligned tail accuracy, original-model Bellman struc-
ture, completed-incumbent improvement and paid stopping. The remaining-gain
rule has an explicit economic meaning: omitted computation can sacrifice at most a
verified amount of original-policy improvement. Its recursive extension requires
a comparator-future residual and risk-distorted propagation, not an unqualified
average of physical state frequencies.
The original investment comparison executes that trade-off with common infor-
mation and strong conventional controls. It records substantial savings in support
and certification work, strictly improved fitted policies relative to completed plain
incumbents, and the small but sometimes positive cost of stopping earlier than
the full safeguard. Exact ReLU–hinge policy equivalence and the competitiveness
of quadratic, spline and semi-analytic methods remain visible. No internal fitting
metric or favorable timing subset is substituted for original economic loss.

utility BSDE bridge makes one rigorous connection to NDU/FBSDE research with-
out transferring results across objectives or information structures. Current success-
ful computations and complete proofs do not close those broader claims, nor do the
preserved negative results replace their pursuit. The original NBO identity and the
economic and numerical-methods ambition are retained.

APPENDIX BK: RETAINED ORIGINAL-OWNER COMPILATION AND ACQUIRED
CONSTRUCTION
BK.1. Original-owner compilation on a tensor cover
On a tensor cover X = ∏d
j=1{xj,0, . . ., xj,nj}, put S = ∏j(nj + 1). For arbitrary
labels yi, including inconsistent inexact labels, compute at each grid node v
(zv, ov) = min
lex,i (yi + L∥v −xi∥1,i).
The index ov is the original label owner, not the transformed node v.
THEOREM A.24—Continuous original-owner identity: For a closed tensor cell C
with corners V(C), and x ∈C,
f (x) = min
v∈V(C)(zv + L∥x −v∥1),
(A.62)
( f (x),i∗(x)) =
min
lex,v∈V(C)(yov + L∥x −xov∥1, ov).

comparisons and O(S) storage. After locating the cell, a query uses O(d2d) arithmetic
operations. Exact rational comparisons preserve all ties, including L = 0. Using the original
owner’s repaired action preserves the uncompiled policy, its cost and its certificate exactly.
The proof is in Supplement, Section Q.3.
The nodal algorithm is the classical distance transform (Felzenszwalb and Hut-
tenlocher, 2012); preserving the original action through continuous off-grid queries
is the policy obligation. If there are Jt,i node actions and Mt integration represen-
tatives, write Qt = Mt ∑i Jt,i. Literal dense cone evaluation costs O(∑t dSt+1Qt) in
representation work. Compilation replaces this by O(∑t[dSt+1 + Qtd2d]), plus cell
location, primitive evaluation, integration, feasible repair, certificate and output.
Rational bit lengths and state boxes crossing many cells incur additional costs. There
is no dimension-free complexity assertion.

original action to the smallest capacity throughout that cell and round down to an
action quantum ∆t. This is feasible at every state in the cell. Relative to an exact
true-state repair, its displacement is at most 2KA

APPENDIX BL: RETAINED RESIDUAL SCREENING AND PROSPECTIVE
FINITE-MENU SELECTION
BL.1. Residual covers and strict continuum screening
A cellwise residual bracket need not solve another action problem at every state.
On each rectangular state cell, convex interpolation of the vertex upper values
dominates V1; each affine function (17) minorizes it globally. The same interpolation
and subgradient construction applies to convex f . Comparing an affine minorant of
one function with the convex interpolation upper bound of the other at every vertex
proves a bound for V1 −f throughout the cell. Taking the best available anchor and
then the worst cell gives a whole-domain residual interval. The 32 × 32 cover below
therefore qualifies the continuous square, rather than converting its 1,089 nodes
into empirical generalization observations.
Let [li, ui] enclose an original successor value over every point of bin Bi. If τ is
the kth largest li, k = n(1 −α), then
ui < τ
(A.64)
excludes all risk mass from bin i in an upper-tail maximizer. At least 1 −α of
the original probability mass has value at least τ; strict separation makes any
positive mass on the excluded bin suboptimal. Equality is retained. These bounds
must be available before screening. The screening calculation below pays for their
construction and for the test itself, and compares identical upper-tail values with

BL.2. Which training loss controls rejection?
Fix a finite menu H of M complete candidate services before validation. Each
candidate specifies its proposal, rounding, certificate algorithm and fallback. On a
context x, its first proposal is accepted when the valid complete-policy certificate
Γh(x) is at most τ > 0. For a one-date problem, (A.2) is such a certificate. At multiple
dates it must additionally include the certified future-policy allowance. Define
Rh(x) = 1{Γh(x) > τ},
ℓh(x) = min{1, Γh(x)/τ}.
(A.65)
Then Rh ≤ℓh. Equality at the admission boundary is accepted. A valid fallback com-
pletes every rejected context; discarding it would change the service and invalidate
its resource comparison.

For an empirical minimizer of ℓh, the same event instead gives ERbh ≤minh Eℓh + 2en.

The work statement means EWbh ≤C0 + C1(minh ERh + 2en) for the rejection
selector, and analogously for ℓ. A measured maximum is not a verified Wmax, and
a rejection-optimal selector need not minimize runtime when fallback costs differ
across contexts. On the finite dyadic domain used by the investment service, a finite
fallback can supply a worst-case operation cap; its size, rather than a favorable ob-
served clock, enters this theorem. Conditional concentration allows data-dependent
acquisition, but does not allow the menu or certificate rule to be changed after
looking at the validation sample.
Theorems A.1–A.25 provide the missing distinction between optimizing a resid-
ual certificate and optimizing an action-relevant quantity. They do not retroactively
certify the empirical performance of the R97 residual objective, or supply observa-
tions for the separately frozen R98 actors. Decision-aware prediction and surrogate
calibration are established ideas (Elmachtoub and Grigas, 2022, Liu and Grigas,
2021). Here the loss is attached to an outward original-law, all-action Bellman cer-
tificate and a complete feasible service. The finite-menu concentration argument
is classical; the support-to-admission construction specifies what that argument is
permitted to select.
APPENDIX BM: A REMOTELY FROZEN, DECISION-SCALE COMPARISON
The new comparison follows the complete-service definition of Theorem A.30.
It is not a relabeling of the R95 actors. Oblique ReLU, adaptive coordinate-spline
and projected-quadratic continuations have three nonlinear features and three
affine coefficients. Each fitted design has rank six, uses 1,024 common original-risk
training labels, and occupies an identical 128-byte executable encoding. Forward
selection considers the same number of candidates and uses identical optimization
stopping parameters. Every candidate fit, rank rejection and selected feature is
retained. Effective design rank is reported separately from nonzero readout count
and conditioning. Equal nominal or solver-call budgets do not imply equal fitting
time.

Construction and complete work.
Label construction, all feature-search fits, state-
cover qualification, calibration, serialization and reload are recorded separately for
each representation. A model’s standalone purchase bears the full shared label cost
rather than an arbitrary one-third allocation. Five fresh processes per arm and risk
level evaluate the same fixed 32-state timing workload; the parent timer includes
interpreter startup, identity checking, loading, qualification, output and shutdown.
CPU frequency is recorded, not controlled. Timing ranges are descriptive and feed
a conditional sensitivity region, not a confidence interval for future hardware. One-
time independent audit cost is shown separately and can be included explicitly in
the acquisition charge.
Prospective certificate ablation.
The builders of the global norm, signed scalar and
joint local-support bounds are fixed before confirmation, with the same residual
cover and own-continuation resolution. Their proposed-policy identities remain
explicit. A scalar bound for a rejected fitted proposal is not attached to the service’s
different fallback action. The comparison records qualification failures and paid
construction work, while distinguishing these fixed builders from a separately
tuned solver frontier. The earlier screening experiment and its negative net-time
result remain unchanged.
Independent endpoints.
The independent implementation uses exact rational arith-
metic for all paired means and coverage constants. It does not import the production
statistical formula. It also chooses eight random rows from each arm–risk stratum,
reconstructs the stored candidate actions, and forms a finer original-law complete-
policy enclosure and an original-action lower witness from separately written
economic primitives. The finer interval must be contained in the reported one.

APPENDIX BN: ACQUIRING AND QUALIFYING NEURAL READOUTS
The new experiment asks whether a construction directed at a valid residual ac-
count improves the delivered service, and whether any improvement is attributable
to neural geometry. The two questions require separate controls. There are seven
services: conventional online risk-DP, and least-squares (LS) and certificate-oriented
(CA) readouts for each of the quadratic, oblique-ReLU, and coordinate-spline fam-
ilies. The risk levels remain 1/2 and 3/4. Design ranks are four, five, and six;
training-label budgets are 256 and 1,024. The resulting 84 configurations are fixed
in a remotely committed protocol before the campaign.
Within a family–budget cell the two readouts use identical selected geometry
and have the same available original-model labels. Both pay for the 1,089-site cover,
including repeated primitive queries used by whole-domain validation. The CA
procedure solves (A.78), rounds its actual coefficients, and applies Proposition A.34.
The family tag, feature directions, offsets, and readout coefficients occupy 64, 96,
or 128 bytes at ranks four, five, or six, respectively. All feature-search trials and
rank rejections remain in the receipts; matching design rank does not imply equal
conditioning or equal fitting work.
Each cell has 16 service-validation states and 64 paired diagnostic states. The
complete controller and admission targets are unchanged from R96, not retuned
to make CA appear successful. Its stage record distinguishes proposal generation,

Acquisition and a purchase.
A fresh acquisition process starts from economic prim-

process cost; the full process, including imports, file output, durable serialization
and a subsequent diagnostic probe, supplies a conservative upper endpoint. This
deliberately broad bracket avoids subtracting a noisy probe timer to manufacture a
small setup cost. It includes repeated labels and any unsuccessful candidate con-
struction. Research authoring and the separate referee reimplementation are not
silently part of a purported deployment microbenchmark: their execution receipts
are provided separately, and a purchaser requiring an additional audit must add its
charge to acquisition or the fixed fee.

APPENDIX BP: DECISION-SCALE PRECISION AND THE COST OF A QUALIFIED
NBO
An approximation can save continuation queries and still leave an economic
comparison unresolved. The investment experiment in Section CB illustrates this
distinction: the original policy intervals establish equivalence only at a margin equal
to four fifths of the maximal first-date investment charge. We now connect numerical
integration, policy admission, statistical resolution and the cost of deployment. The
original economic law and the NBO construction remain the benchmark. Neither
a smaller numerical interval nor a new admission rule is silently attributed to the
unchanged historical actor.

BP.2. Admission changes the statistical support
A stored continuation first proposes an action. A qualified service accepts that ac-
tion only when its complete-policy bound is at most τ against the original optimum.
Otherwise it pays for the declared conventional action and verifies that action. An
exact finite-cover fallback makes this a complete measurable service on the declared
dyadic initial domain, rather than a controller defined only on successful sample
rows. The fallback is part of the policy, and a rejected proposed action remains in
the record.

BP.3. Acquisition, reuse and an economic purchase
Let Ka be a one-time acquisition charge for service a, and ca its cost per future
workload. The acquisition account includes labels, feature search, fitting, validation,
serialization and the chosen audit campaign. A fresh-process workload includes
loading, identity checks, action proposal, admission, fallback, numerical certifica-
tion, output and shutdown. Let a workload contain B initial-state decisions and let
d = E[Ja −Jb] be the per-decision original policy-cost contrast, λ ≥0 the price of
computational work in the same normalized cost units, and F an additional fixed
fee difference. For m future workloads, the total normalized difference is
m{Bd + λ(ca −cb)} + λ(Ka −Kb) + F.
(A.75)
For the recorded timing workloads B = 32; for a single decision B = 1. This expres-
sion distinguishes a policy-quality loss from the value of saved computation. A
price is not inferred from seconds, a coefficient count, or an integration bin.

PROPOSITION A.31—Robust acquisition-and-reuse region: Suppose the policy
contrast has simultaneous upper bound d+, the workload saving cb −ca has a valid lower
bound s−, and the incremental acquisition and fee have upper bounds k+ and F+. Then
service a weakly improves total normalized cost whenever
m(λs−−Bd+) ≥λk+ + F+.
(A.76)
If λs−−Bd+ > 0 and the right side is nonnegative, the smallest sufficient integer workload
count is its ratio rounded upward. If the denominator is nonpositive and the right side is
positive, no positive workload count is certified by these bounds. Separately, a purchaser’s
quality condition is d+ ≤ϵ; it must not be inferred from a positive computational saving.
The timing repetitions below produce descriptive machine-specific ranges, not
probabilistic guarantees for arbitrary future machines. Inserting their extrema in
(A.76) gives a sensitivity calculation conditional on that timing envelope. It does
not turn five repeated processes into a confidence bound on long-run prices or
runtime. The theorem states the economic decision that adequately measured cost
bounds would license, while the experimental record states precisely which costs
were observed.
APPENDIX BQ: INFORMATION, REPRESENTATION, AND THE PRICE OF A
COMPLETE POLICY
The validity of a Bellman comparison and the usefulness of its neural representa-
tion are different mathematical questions. Original-model qualification answers the
first. The approximation class, its acquisition cost, and the work of rejected propos-
als answer the second. This section sharpens the distinction without changing the
policy-construction problem.

has no derivative oracle, functional formula, or uncharged continuation labels. Its

deterministic information exponent is two.
The proof constructs two convex continuations with the same adaptive tran-
script but different tail integrals. It is given in the supplement rather than inferred
from the sharpness of a particular quadrature rule. This is an information-class
statement, whereas the earlier two-ReLU construction attains the constant of the
specified midpoint–endpoint pair. Neither statement establishes a constant optimal
uniformly in α, a randomized lower bound, or a dimension-independent bound.

The argument uses classical information-based lower-bound reasoning, not a
claim that indistinguishable-input arguments originate here; see Novak (2015).
Likewise, the AVaR variational representation is due to Rockafellar and Uryasev
(2000). The contribution here is the explicit convex-Lipschitz tail construction, its
admissible information class, and its connection to the certified recursive-policy
resolution problem. Convexity of a class of inputs is not the same as convexity of
each input function; the proof does not invoke a theorem requiring a balanced class.

BQ.2. What a neural representation can contribute
A representation-neutral verifier does not imply representation-neutral approxi-
mation cost. The following comparison isolates one elementary source of a neural
advantage and one limit to that interpretation.
PROPOSITION A.33—An oblique continuation: On [0,1]2, let v(x) = (x1 + x2 −
1)+. A single oblique ReLU represents v exactly. The best uniform approximation errors
from arbitrary additive functions a(x1) + b(x2) and from polynomials of total degree at
most two are, respectively, 1/4 and 1/16.
This is a structural example in the continuation class, not a claim that the in-
vestment value function equals this ridge, that its action loss equals its value-
approximation error, or that every conventional method is separated. A conven-
tional method with the same oblique hinge also represents it exactly. Consequently,
the identifiable object is acquired geometry, rather than the name attached to an
equivalent formula. In the investment experiment the quadratic arm remains the
observed computational winner. The proposition explains why that result neither
proves a universal quadratic advantage nor supplies evidence of a neural advantage
in that particular application.
For the investment continuations, write a fixed-feature readout as hθ(z) = ϕ(z)′θ.
At acquired sites zi, the original-model computation gives V(zi) ∈[ℓi, ui]. An
interval-aware construction solves
min

subject to
ϕ(zi)′θ + l ≤ℓi,

for every i. (A.78)
Nonnegative nonlinear coefficients preserve convexity; the constant coefficient can
be fixed because residual span is invariant to an additive constant. Numerical
feasibility of this finite program is not itself a certificate on the state domain.

BQ.3. A workload-consistent purchase frontier
Let a be a candidate complete policy service and b its comparator. The per-
decision policy-cost difference is d = E[Ja −Jb]. A purchased workload contains B
initial-state decisions; ca, cb are seconds per whole workload, and Ka, Kb are one-time
acquisition seconds. Let λ ≥0 be a price in normalized model-cost units per second
and F ≥0 an additional adoption fee. For m workloads, the gain from choosing a is
G(m) = m{λ(cb −ca) −Bd} −λ(Ka −Kb) −F.
(A.80)
The factor B is essential: a cost estimate for one initial state cannot be combined
directly with the clock of a 32-state process.
THEOREM A.35—Interval purchase decisions: Suppose jointly valid bounds are d ∈
[d−, d+], cb −ca ∈[s−, s+], Ka −Kb ∈[k−, k+], and F ∈[F−, F+]. Then, simultaneously
for every integer m ≥1 and λ ≥0,
G−(m) = m(λs−−Bd+) −λk+ −F+ ≤G(m),
(A.81)
G(m) ≤m(λs+ −Bd−) −λk−−F−= G+(m).
(A.82)

probability bounds for future clocks: a frontier using those ranges is conditional
on their continued applicability. The economic accounting is exact; the empirical
strength of its inputs remains an independently assessable question.

The polytope is closed and bounded: mt, qt are subprobabilities or probabilities,
0 ≤y ≤1, and z is bounded by its nonnegative row sum. It is nonempty whenever
the qualification class is nonempty, in particular when it contains bθ. Hence its
extrema exist. Adding valid constraints shrinks it. If a smaller tolerance retains all
larger-tolerance constraints and possibly more, its lower extremum increases and its
upper extremum decreases. Independent dual feasibility supplies the appropriate
weak-duality bound even when the numerical solve is incomplete. Adding and
subtracting the two reference costs proves the class comparison. These operations
are deterministic on the simultaneous input event.
Why reference weights are insufficient.
Consider a two-date, zero-stage-cost exam-
ple. Initially only state s is visited. At date zero, action L moves to state ℓand R to
state r. At date one the costly action costs one at r and zero at ℓ. The reference selects
L; a candidate selects R and then the costly action at r. The reference’s date-one
occupation gives r mass zero, but the candidate’s cost difference is one. A first-date
formula using the reference continuation sees zero date-zero contrast and omits the
later change. The flow constraint instead forces m1r = 1 and charges the date-one
advantage. This example identifies an error that cannot be repaired by a union
bound over cells.
Shared coefficients remain material.
In the same example, let θ ∈{−1,1}. At s
action R has score −θ and L score zero; at r the costly action has score θ and the free
action score zero. Each event is individually possible, but R and the costly action
require opposite signs. Every common-parameter policy has cost zero, whereas
the unconstrained action relaxation permits cost one. The exact conflict inequality
excludes their simultaneous integral choice. Its fractional relaxation can still admit
cost 1/2; this is why the theorem asserts validity and monotone tightening, not
exact attainability of every relaxed occupation.

BS.2. Adaptive acquisition coverage
Fix one cover ball B. Let Ei be the event that the first i acquisitions miss it. By the
conditional lower-probability assumption,
Pr(Ei) = E[1Ei−1 Pr(Yi /∈B | Fi−1)] ≤(1 −ah) Pr(Ei−1).
Induction yields (1 −ah)n. A union bound over the M fixed balls gives the result. If
none is missed, any point is within h of a cover center and that center is within h
of an acquired node, hence the radius is 2h. This argument controls geometry, not
label error; any probabilistic label-certification event is included separately in the
overall error allocation. Pure exploitation without a conditional lower-probability
bound does not satisfy the proposition.

BU.2. Price and fee regions
For a compact joint cost polytope D and two feasible assignments x, y, the largest
objective difference is
sup

{λc · (x −y) + p · (wx −wy) + f · (x −y)}

problem; independently choosing the worst endpoint of each pair can be looser. No
step estimates a price, monetary scale or adoption fee from a clock measurement.

The distinction between function and decision error matters. Cash shifts do not
affect an action choice, and even a nonconstant approximation error may preserve
the minimizer. No lower bound for policy regret follows from this proposition
without a further decision construction. In particular, the proposition is not used to
reinterpret the R96 quadratic winner as a neural winner.

Indeed, choose a nearest site and apply the Lipschitz inequality to V −h. Directed
rounding must enclose the displayed arithmetic. The implementation retains the
stronger inherited convex-cell residual construction rather than replacing it by this
generic bound. Its linear program is only a candidate generator; both the baseline
and candidate are evaluated by the same whole-domain validator.
The LP fixes the intercept to zero, bounds the two affine slopes in [−104,104], and
bounds nonlinear coefficients in [0,104]. These are explicit acquisition restrictions,
not claimed characterizations of the best neural approximation. The two residual
endpoints are unrestricted. Setting all readout coefficients to zero and choosing
endpoints to enclose all acquired value intervals is feasible, so a solver failure is an
execution failure, not evidence that the mathematical program is infeasible. The re-
tained nonnegative nonlinear coefficients remain convex after dyadic rounding. All
attempted feature fits, rank rejections, selection ties, and LP iterations are retained
in construction receipts.
BV.4. Proof of Theorem A.35
Subtract total candidate cost m{BEJa + λca} + λKa + F from comparator cost
m{BEJb + λcb} + λKb. This gives (A.80). Monotonicity of this affine expression in
each interval argument, using m, B ≥0 and λ ≥0, gives (A.81)–(A.82). The strict
inequality mq > C is equivalent to m > C/q when q > 0, yielding the first integer
stated in the theorem.

PROPOSITION A.39—Acquisition coverage under persistent exploration: Choose
M deterministic radius-h balls whose centers cover K. If, before each acquisition i, every
such ball has conditional probability at least ah > 0 of containing the next node, then after
n acquisitions the probability that the acquired nodes fail to form a radius-2h cover is at
most M(1 −ah)n ≤M exp(−nah). Thus n ≥[log M + log(1/δ)]/ah is sufficient. The
assertion permits an adaptive acquisition law satisfying the conditional lower bound; it
does not silently replace such a law by IID sampling. On the coverage event, Theorem A.38
applies with ht = 2h, provided the own-future labels and primitive moduli have their stated
simultaneous certification.
BY.1. From approximation to predictor work

upper endpoint does not exceed every competitor’s lower endpoint. Let ∆be the
true best-to-second-best gap, with ∆= 0 for ties.

bounds the optimum of an explicitly stated resource upper model. It is not a lower
bound on the work of every algorithm solving the economic problem.
COROLLARY A.42—A constructive horizon bound with coupled evaluation: Sup-
pose wt = 1, ε/T ≤min{1,mint ¯ηt}, J ≤KT, cj ≤C, and the total degrees are bounded
by a fixed P. Then a feasible stored-continuation implementation satisfies
F∗≤F0 + KC TP+1ε−P.
For a dense successor account with label exponent p and evaluation exponent s, the adjacent-
date term has degree p + s. Thus a valid polynomial horizon account charges p + s, rather
than silently holding the successor cost constant. Worsening regularity, growing cover
dimension, bit lengths and setup remain explicit inputs; none is bounded by this corollary
without its stated hypotheses.

Policy and resource certificates.
Qualification determines which policy outputs
meet the economic accuracy requirement. The coupled program determines how a
specified implementation distributes the corresponding dated allowances. These are
different optimizations. A tight resource certificate cannot replace an original-law
policy certificate, and a tight policy certificate does not determine hardware time.
Keeping both accounts explicit permits constructive improvement without a claim
of dimension-free or universally faster computation.
APPENDIX CA: PROSPECTIVE CHOICE AND ECONOMICALLY INTERPRETABLE

Exact ranking on a completed catalogue and preference before a new workload
are different claims. We connect them by a population selection bound and a
separately frozen evaluation, retaining the original investment economy and every
comparator.

construction of m complete services, each with original-law cost in [0, H]. For n independent

and qn = H

fixed tie rule. Here λ ≥0, p ≥0, and the nonrandom resource and fee inputs are declared

its expected objective regret is at most

CA.2. Uniform price-fee sensitivity
Let X be a finite set of feasible service assignments, including the original capacity
constraints. Let D be a nonempty compact polytope containing their joint normal-
ized cost vector. For an assignment x, let wx be its complete resource vector, λ ≥0
the value of normalized policy loss, p ≥0 the resource prices, and f the assignment
fee vector. All coordinates refer to explicit units. Put hD(v) = supc∈D c · v.
PROPOSITION A.44—Uniform purchase region: Assignment x is optimal for every
cost vector in D exactly on the region
Rx =

(A.93)

CB.1. Frozen design and common accuracy
Each risk level has 1,024 training states, 128 calibration states and 2,048 evaluation
states. The three streams are domain-separated before execution. States are drawn
from the declared uniform 20-bit dyadic initial-state distribution; the state dynamics
and innovations between decisions remain continuous. Each fitted arm uses the
same labels, 32 fixed nonlinear features, an unrestricted affine part and nonnegative
nonlinear coefficients. Least squares uses the same solver tolerance and iteration
cap; readouts are stored on a 30-bit dyadic grid. The source, serialized coefficients
and calibration selector are checked before evaluation. No fitting or reselection
occurs on the evaluation stream.
The selector minimizes calibration mean cost-interval midpoints with a fixed
lexicographic tie rule. It chooses online risk-DP at both risk levels. All twelve
pairwise comparisons across the two levels were specified in advance, including
those not involving the selected arm. The independent observation is an initial state,
not a shock bin or a repeated solver query.
A common own-continuation gap is insufficient for a fair policy comparison.
We require both an own-continuation gap at most 1/64 and an original-optimum
complete-policy loss bound at most 1/16 at every queried initial state. Fitted arms
pay for the extra original-continuation lower witness in Theorem 5; online risk-DP
reuses its already computed witness. Integration may refine from 128 to 4,096 bins,
but the proposed first action cannot change. All failures are retained rather than
silently replaced by conventional actions. The terminal controller is common to
every arm and has the uniform allowance proved above.
