target. This is a statement about every recorded initial state, not an empirical proof
of that same tolerance on all possible initial states. The separate residual cover
qualifies the whole continuous state square.

These measurements identify a benefit of stored continuations on this workload,
not a uniquely neural advantage. Spline and quadratic continuations obtain similar
execution reductions, and the fitted arms are not rank matched. The counts identify

result.
Whole-bin screening excludes between 738 and 746 of 4,096 candidates at α = 1/2,
and between 2,053 and 2,062 at α = 3/4. After paying for unpruned original-value
bounds and the strict test, the screened calculation is slightly slower in every
displayed case. The exact unchanged tail values validate the exclusions; they do
not establish a computational gain. No-cut rows and all denominators are retained
in the appendix. The experiment therefore separates a valid geometric certificate,
the amount it removes and the net value of constructing it.
The two-date scalar-control experiment does not replace the inherited two-control,
two-innovation horizon frontier. Proposition A.37 now gives explicit fixed-accuracy
resolutions and a horizon-uniform construction for both the scalar and original
vector economies. The general NBO construction and joint-domain theorem remain
available under their hypotheses, while a full independent largest-vector imple-
mentation remains a separate numerical obligation. This distinction preserves the
general research program without borrowing scalability evidence from a different
problem.

A shallow rational affine–ReLU continuation has the form

The operation count does not bound rational bit complexity. Near-zero projected

rational evaluation, including the zero-radius branches, is required. The executed
moment catalogue checks the rational identities against an independently written
polygon integral. It is a conditional-integration experiment, not a new trained-policy
cost comparison. The formulas do not imply that the achieved residual oscillation
of an arbitrary fitted network is small.

CC.3. Qualifying a fitted continuation without a Bellman tree
Uniform qualification need not query V∗. Suppose Qh

action with constants Lx,t, La,t, and ht has constant Lh,t, all in ℓ1. In the investment

displacement at most κ∥x −y∥1, where κ = 1/(8d). Thus a valid residual Lipschitz
constant is

endpoint; the smallest upper endpoint is an upper bound. Exact moments can

true-value curvature minorant for Qh.
For Nt state-cover points and At actions per point, this qualification costs
O(∑t NtAtKt+1d) arithmetic operations, plus certification of the moduli and any
actor-specific greedy-gap bound. Its cover can still be expensive in high dimension.
The result replaces a recursive optimal-value oracle by an explicit approximation-
and-qualification tradeoff; it does not make that qualification free. The residual-
cover proof, the action-mesh argument and the terminal allowance are given in the
supplement. Value-function control variates have an established variance-reduction
literature (Munos, 2006); the additional requirement here is an original-law, whole-
domain certificate for the fitted NBO continuation and the actual acquired policy.

comparison of qualified approximations, not an assertion that different bases span
the same functions or that a neural encoding has an intrinsic advantage.
APPENDIX CE: REPRESENTATION CALIBRATION AND OPTIMIZATION-STABLE

The attained continuation in Section CC is an economic object, not merely an
optional action proposal. Its qualification must charge the represented function
rather than an avoidable featurewise overestimate. We make this comparison ex-
plicit and then pass from an attained fit to a class of optimization outputs with the
same implemented policy. All statements in this section retain the original two-date
investment law, fixed terminal payoff, acquired cells and feasible action menus.

PROPOSITION A.48—Affine-exact qualification: The moduli in (A.104)–(A.105)
give valid residual enclosures and the residual-oscillation upper bound (A.106). The objec-
tive is convex and admits a finite linear-programming representation. For every common
affine continuation h(x) = a + ux1 + vx2, whenever its two coefficient representations are
feasible, both moduli equal max{|u|,|v|}. Thus, for common labels, node cover and target
modulus, the two qualification objectives agree on this affine function.
PROOF: A ReLU coordinate has the displayed cumulative slopes on its four affine
intervals. The dual norm of ℓ1 is ℓ∞, so their largest coordinate magnitude gives
the state modulus. A Bernstein derivative is a convex combination of 4(θij −θi,j−1)
with degree-three Bernstein weights. This proves its bound. Residuals change by
at most (G + L)ρ between a node and a covered state, proving the enclosure and
its oscillation bound. Each term in (A.106) is a maximum of finitely many affine
functions. For an affine function, the ReLU coefficients are (u,0,0,0) and (v,0,0,0);
the Bernstein coefficients are (u/4, u/2,3u/4, u) and the analogous vector for v. All
relevant slopes or derivative controls are u or v.

Any critic-minimizing action b ̸= aC satisfies gCb(θ) ≤0, so DCb ≤
F(θ) ≤U + ϵ. It therefore belongs to (A.111). Conditioning on the initial cell ex-
presses the policy-cost difference as ∑C pC∆C(bC(θ)), which is between the end-
points in (A.112). The infimum of F is at most U, giving the optimization conclusion.
A cell retaining only aC contributes zero; the signed support bounds every other
contribution. Finally add and subtract the two attained costs to obtain (A.114). All
steps after the attained-policy event are deterministic.
Q.E.D.

The cellwise extrema relax the common-coefficient restriction and need not be
attained by one readout. The theorem is consequently not a sharp joint characteriza-
tion of the optimizer class. Its useful feature is different: it can retain an identified
economic comparison when some actions remain uncertified and the binary Hqϵ
allowance is too large. The original Bellman optimum and the constructive accuracy
results are unchanged. A reference expected-loss upper bound can also be enlarged
by vϵ; the actionwise comparison itself is not a new bound obtained by replacing
the original optimum with a menu optimum.
For the executed two-date economy, the conditional contrasts are computed from
the original stage costs, transitions and fixed terminal actor. Common innovations
preserve their actual marginal laws. Centered polynomial differences retain cancella-
tion, and rectangle queries enclose every crossed acquired cell. The final innovation
is integrated analytically. Appendix DR proves whole-bin validity, deterministic
refinement convergence under vanishing arithmetic error, and the work bound.
It also separates integration accuracy from the independent statistical interval to
which (A.114) is applied.

about neural fitting success.
APPENDIX CH: COMMON READOUTS AND ECONOMIC POLICY QUALIFICATION
An approximately optimized continuation is one function. Its coefficients deter-
mine the action in every observation cell. Separate action-switch tests deliberately
forget part of this structure: an alternative may defeat the reference action without
winning the complete feasible menu, and individually possible choices need not be
jointly generated by the same readout. We retain these restrictions when transfer-
ring the original NBO qualification account to an economic decision. The attained
continuation, economic primitives, action menu and policy-cost observations are
unchanged.

Computation and scope.
The number of complete patterns can be exponential in
the number of dated cells. Enumeration is therefore a finite exact implementation,
not a general polynomial-time claim. One may begin with an outer covering of
parameter space, retain every unresolved pattern and refine only economically
material branches. Every discarded branch needs a valid exclusion for the actual
own-future qualification functional. Missing a branch invalidates the bound; retain-
ing an unresolved branch only weakens it. The state-flow width in (A.125) and the
global-pattern relaxation are distinct approximation costs. This distinction preserves
both the original continuous economy and the original-optimum policy sandwich
while making the added qualification work explicit.
APPENDIX CJ: ORIGINAL-LAW QUALIFICATION UNDER TRANSPORT

The occupation bounds retain a complete policy and its induced state distribution.
Their cellwise convergence result, however, requires shrinking transition-probability
widths. Moving a deterministic successor by an arbitrarily small distance need
not make those widths small. We develop a complementary certificate that tests
the transition approximation against the actual stored continuation. It applies to
singular as well as diffuse transition laws and does not require a continuous greedy
actor.

is supplied. Write B0 = 1 and Bt = ∏s<t βs, where βs ≥0. A parameter θ determines
all stored continuations ft,θ and a complete feasible policy πθ. Parameters, actions
and continuations can be shared across dates and economic contexts; the state
includes every endogenous variable needed by the original model.

The full proof is in Supplement EP. It compares the candidate and the original
Bellman optimum separately to the same stored continuation, before subtracting
their bounds. Applying a baseline occupation law to a different complete policy is
neither necessary nor valid. The use of a uniform continuation modulus is essen-
tial: a small transport distance alone does not control integration of an arbitrary
discontinuous value function.
What the representation contributes.
For the constructed affine–ReLU continua-
tions, a valid Lipschitz modulus follows either from the cone construction or from
verified layer norms. The resulting Kt+1 prices transition approximation in the
policy certificate. The exact same function represented by a native minimum circuit
has the same mathematical guarantee. The result identifies the role of the neural
continuation without making a method-neutral verifier evidence of universal neural
speed. Wasserstein robustness and finite-model approximation have established
analyses (Zhou et al., 2024, Saldi et al., 2015); our use is the uniform, translation-
invariant qualification account for shared NBO continuations and their complete
original-law policies.

A singular-transition diagnostic.
Take one decision date, β = 1, terminal cost
g(x) = x on [0,1], and actions 0 and 1. Action 0 has zero immediate cost and true
successor h > 0; action 1 costs h/2 and has successor zero. The numerical kernel
places both successors at zero. With f0 = 0 and f1 = g, its greedy choice is action 0, its
residual span is zero and its true regret is h/2. Omitting the transition charge would
falsely certify zero regret. The transport certificate is 2h and converges to zero, while
the total-variation distance for action 0 is one for every h > 0. Appendix DY gives
exact rational checks. This diagnostic is not a new observation in the investment
experiment.
APPENDIX CK: SEQUENTIAL QUALIFICATION OF POLICY COSTS
A fixed-sample interval does not by itself justify repeated inspection until a
controller appears acceptable. Nor do cost observations from changing controllers
identify the last controller’s cost. We extend the frozen-continuation identity to
predictable episodes and distinguish these targets. This uses established time-
uniform concentration principles (Howard et al., 2020); confidence sequences have
also been used for gated deployment in contextual bandits (Karampatziakis et al.,
2021). Here the observations are verified, continuous-law NBO cost contrasts, not
importance-weighted bandit rewards.

Each endpoint may also be intersected with the corresponding average predictable support
endpoint. The assertion holds at every almost surely finite stopping time. If the complete
controller pair and initial-law/reset contract stay fixed, then ∆i = ∆, even when the qualified

The proof applies conditional Hoeffding bounds to each endpoint and Ville’s
inequality to a finite collection of nonnegative supermartingales. It requires no
independent or identically distributed deployment contexts. It does require the
stated conditional transition laws. Within-episode cache adaptation is allowed only
when the controllers are treated as history-dependent algorithms and the greedy-
gap qualification covers every memory state that can occur. Repeating the same
program identifier while carrying a different cache state does not establish a fixed
conditional target.
The implementation uses a finite dyadic collection of λj and exact rational upper
bounds for the logarithms. These give conservative, computable versions of (A.131).
It reserves the support and target identity before accepting an episode. A failed
numerical evaluation consumes the full previously qualified support interval and
its actual work; it is not deleted after inspecting its outcome. A failure of the support
certificate itself stops qualification.

explicit decision inputs. The number of qualification episodes is not automatically

let the original investment decision use a valid stopping rule without silently
changing either its estimand or its units.
APPENDIX CL: ORIGINAL-LAW QUALIFICATION OF CONSTRUCTED POLICIES
A continuation can have a verified fitting objective without its implemented
policy having an identified economic advantage. The distinction is resolved by
evaluating the same complete policy that the construction returns. We now connect
the qualification-optimal readouts of Section CD to independent original-law cost
observations. Neither the fitted future nor the acquired actor is replaced during
evaluation. The comparison concerns the constructed NBO policies, rather than a
different recursive controller supplied with the same neural label.

An initial or innovation bin is a continuous cell, not a point mass. The evalua-

enclosure, and every resulting feasible action. When an enclosure crosses an acqui-
sition boundary, all intersected actions enter the continuation enclosure. A second
implementation evaluates the same primitives using integer-directed arithmetic
and expanded polynomials. The reported endpoints are the hull of the two valid
enclosures, intersected with the proved support. Arithmetic agreement is a check
on the implementations; validity follows from the enclosure rules and the primitive
identities, not from agreement alone.

Precision, equivalence and improvement are different conclusions. For a cost-
difference interval [l, u] and a predeclared margin δ, equivalence requires −δ < l ≤
u < δ. Noninferiority of the first policy requires u < δ; strict superiority requires
u < 0. An interval can meet its width target and fail equivalence because it identifies
a material difference. These decisions are made from exact endpoints, not from
rounded table entries.
COROLLARY A.59—Priced selection and adoption: On the simultaneous event of
Theorem A.58, let [Lj,Uj] qualify the cost of policy j, and let wj be its declared nonnegative
resource charge. A minimizer bj of Uj + wj satisfies, for every policy j,
Jbj + wbj ≤Jj + wj + (Uj −Lj).
The inequality holds for every assignment of resource prices on the same event. If the gain
from replacing an installed controller is in [l, u], then m deployments, monetary scale v ≥0,
qualification charge q ≥0 and replacement fee f ≥0 give expected net benefit in
[mvl −q −f, mvu −q −f ].
In particular, when l > 0 and v > 0, every m > (q + f )/(vl) is certified beneficial.
PROOF: The first assertion follows from Jbj ≤Ubj, the minimizing property, and
Uj ≤Jj + Uj −Lj. These deterministic inequalities hold for all nonnegative prices
once all cost intervals cover. The second assertion is multiplication by mv and
subtraction of q + f .
Q.E.D.

losses. An already paid construction and a prospective purchase have different
charges. When only a shared qualification service has been timed, charging that

CL.3. The constructed-controller experiment
The fixed catalogue consists of the four previously constructed NBO actors and
the admissible zero-investment incumbent. ReLU and degree-four Bernstein con-
tinuations each have nine coefficients and are constructed on eight- or sixteen-cell
coordinate covers. At a fixed cover, the two bases use the same acquisition con-
tract and primitive information. The actor arrays, actual fitted futures and exact
optimization certificates are unchanged. The zero-investment policy supplies an
economically interpretable installed reference; it is not substituted for the strong
conventional query competitors in the preceding study.
Before execution, the protocol fixes N = 524,288, forty-bit continuous bins, the
sample stream, the full-width target 1/256, and the separate two-sided equivalence
margin 1/256. All five marginal costs and ten paired differences are reported for
both observations in (A.133)–(A.134). Thus K = 30 and ℓ= 10 give a joint failure
bound below 1/100. Reusing a row for another controller or estimator does not
increase the independent sample count. The declared independence model concerns
the simulated rows; a fixed pseudorandom seed establishes reproducibility, not
mathematical independence.
Outcomes of the fixed precision design.
Across both estimators, 20 of the twenty
paired intervals meet the declared full-width target. Their widths range from
0.000936 to 0.002285. Exactly 4 meet the separate equivalence criterion. Neither a
failed width target nor a failed equivalence comparison is omitted.
The conditionally integrated comparisons identify a positive gain over the zero-
investment incumbent for 4 of the four constructed policies. These are gains of
complete implemented controllers, not reductions in a qualification objective.
At the two matched acquisition resolutions, the ReLU-minus-Bernstein compar-
isons identify 2 lower-cost ReLU outcomes, 0 higher-cost outcomes, and 0 unre-
solved signs. This finite comparison is not a universal representation ranking.

APPENDIX CM: QUALIFICATION, REPRESENTATION, AND ATTAINED ECONOMIC
COST
The preceding attained-controller experiment used a coefficientwise qualifica-
tion bound. Its ReLU–Bernstein ordering is an observation about those specified
constructions. We now examine whether that ordering persists after the two bases
receive the same qualification charge on their common affine functions. This directly
tests a source of representation-dependent conservatism while preserving the origi-
nal nonlinear investment economy and the Neural Bellman Operator construction.
CM.1. A prospective factorial comparison
The design fixes two bases, two qualification rules and two acquisition resolutions.
The eight constructed controllers and the installed zero controller are evaluated on
the same original-law paths. Each basis has nine coefficients with absolute bounds
eight, the same node covers, thirty-three-action search menus and downward
action quantum 1/4096. The calibrated rule replaces the coefficientwise modulus

CM.2. Precision of the economic comparison
The target was a paired total width of 1/256, fixed before seeing the new rows.
Appendix DQ reports every interval and its width components, including every
marginal interval whether or not its width falls below that paired target. Vari-
ance reduction by conditional integration affects the variance component, not the
bounded-support penalty or the acquisition contract. For example, in the fine cali-
brated basis comparison the conditional interval’s width consists of approximately
0.001008605 from the finite-support term, 0.000048152 from endpoint sampling-
variance allowances, and 2.69 × 10−11 from the numerical enclosure. The support
term is therefore the principal remaining contribution in that comparison.
The numerical component includes the implemented handling of continuous-bin
width, acquisition ambiguity and arithmetic propagation. It is not represented as
a pure floating-point error estimate. Likewise, a small numerical component does
not justify dropping the finite-sample support term. These diagnostics explain the
achieved precision without inferring significance from raw mean differences or treat-
ing the inherited R67 policy-cost rows as observations of these newly constructed
actors.
CM.3. From a fitted readout to a qualified optimizer class
For each new terminal-label qualification problem the action-switch catalogue
covers every first-date observation cell and all thirty-two alternative robust actions.
The 20,480 rational dual bounds are independently recomputed using the antideriva-
tive and box-infimum calculations of Appendix DP; no switch optimization is rerun
to replace an unfavorable certificate.
At zero extra objective allowance, the two fine-resolution constructions and coarse
Bernstein have complete first-date action stability. Every exact minimizer of each of
these fixed-label qualification problems therefore gives its attained complete policy,
not merely a similar fitted value. The original-law intervals in Table CM.V extend
to these optimizer classes without additional probability expenditure. The same
conclusion holds for the positive dyadic sublevels displayed in Table CM.IV.

CM.4. Controller choice and complete costs
Both cash and conditional marginal and pair intervals can be used together on
their original simultaneous event. Exact shortest-path closure gives consistent cost
potentials and the pure-choice regret bounds of the inherited decision theorem. The
four-term interactions remain separately reported; sharpness of the pair-constraint
calculation is not asserted after adding those extra restrictions. The complete nine-
controller closure and attaining potentials are deposited in the revision audit.
For the fine calibrated controllers, the positive ReLU-minus-Bernstein interval
determines a nonempty region of additional Bernstein charges for which its lower
policy cost outweighs its extra charge. It also determines the opposite region in
which ReLU is preferred after that charge. All such statements are conditional on
an explicitly supplied conversion of computation, installation and deployment
into normalized cost units. The exact boundary values may be tightened by the
common pair-constraint closure; no new simulation is needed for that deterministic
calculation.
The construction work is recorded rather than presumed equal. Legacy clocks
include a label-loss ablation that the calibrated services do not execute. Their differ-
ence therefore does not identify an end-to-end speed gain from calibration. Exact
action and expected-feature evaluation counts are reported alongside the clocks,
and the original cost-inference, barrier and publication services retain separate mea-
sured costs. The present result supplies an identified policy-cost and conditional
purchase comparison in the original economy. It does not extrapolate a two-date
fitted-continuation calculation into a measured long-horizon speed result for the
recursively queried vector tree.

APPENDIX CO: ECONOMIC VALUE OF COMMON-READOUT QUALIFICATION
The new calculation refines the economic accuracy of the original attained NBO
controllers. It does not fit another controller or change a conditional cost observation.
The four calibrated readouts, their frozen labels, terminal actors, robust 33-action
menus, acquisition grids and original continuous laws are those of the preceding
factorial investment study. The original actionwise integrations and simultaneous
attained-policy intervals remain the paid inputs.
CO.1. A complete, fixed qualification design

only barrier at excess objective at most 2−12 receives a full-menu qualification
problem. This gives 976 problems: 832 for coarse ReLU, nine for coarse Bernstein,
78 for fine ReLU and 57 for fine Bernstein. Each event includes the other 32 feasible
menu actions, with a common coefficient vector and the same objective.
The joint-event design permits at most 512 pairs per model. When at most 128
alternatives remain at the largest allowance, all remaining alternatives seed the pair
catalogue. Otherwise the minimum-lower and maximum-upper conditional-cost
alternatives in each cell seed it. Cross-cell pairs are ranked by the product of their
maximum absolute cost endpoints, with lexicographic tie handling, and the first
512 are retained. The complete roster contains 1572 pairs; the small Bernstein model
contributes all 36 of its possible pairs. This rule is deterministic postprocessing of

CO.3. Complete incremental work and independent arithmetic
The recorded scientific interpreter, including imports, reads, all qualification and
assignment problems, durable outputs and shutdown, takes 104.699 seconds on
the stated ARM runner. Singleton, joint-event and assignment phases are recorded
separately. These measurements price the additional qualification calculation. They
are neither a cold-start cost for rebuilding the original controllers nor a matched
ReLU-versus-Bernstein timing experiment. Original fitting and integration clocks
remain unchanged and must be added when those inputs have not already been
purchased.
A separate rational implementation reconstructs the feature antiderivatives, all
winner comparisons, qualification supports, pair-event separations, conflict rosters
and 16548 assignment inequalities. It checks all 2,548 qualification certificates and
all 36 policy-class comparisons without invoking the production optimizer. Original
R77/R80 continuous-bin and actionwise kernel verification is separately replayed in
the full publication build. The distinction between new exact certificate verification,
inherited full-bin re-integration and independent cost sampling is explicit: this
study adds no new fitting attempt, integration bin or independent cost row.
The economic improvement is consequently a more informative decision from the
original NBO continuation and its previously qualified evidence. Full-menu winner
regions remove alternatives that cannot be selected; common-coefficient restrictions
remove jointly impossible selections; conditional integration prices what remains.

APPENDIX CP: A FROZEN SHARED PROPOSAL ON UNSEEN WORKLOADS
The joint-domain construction in Section BY establishes a mathematical shared-
operator guarantee. A trained proposal’s incremental numerical value is a different
question. We test that value in the original investment model without changing its
continuous innovation law, feasible action cap or protected Bellman certificate. This
experiment adds a prospective comparison to the inherited recursive-query and
complete-policy studies; it does not substitute one of those objects for another.
CP.1. Construction, selection and evaluation
The protocol is fixed before fitting. The training stream contains 128 states in
each of dimensions two and eight, with two remaining dates. Protected adaptive
search at tolerance 1/256 supplies feasible action labels, normalized by the original
action cap. Both approximation families receive the same fourteen features: eight
zero-padded state coordinates, the overall, even-coordinate and odd-coordinate
means, the mean square, the mean adjacent product, and the dimension divided
by eight. The neural model is one width-32 ReLU network shared across both
dimensions. The nonneural comparator is one complete quadratic on the same
features. Each family has one attempted fit and fixed optimization settings, with no
hyperparameter search. All coefficients, training rows and fitting diagnostics are
retained before calibration.
Calibration has 64 new states in each training dimension. The five services are
the adaptive baseline, bisection, a one-date analytic proposal, the shared ReLU
proposal and the shared quadratic proposal. Each runs at tolerance 1/64 using the
unchanged protected oracle. Selection minimizes their total action-value queries,
with the prespecified tie order. A terminal query is already included in that total
and is not added a second time. Calibration selects the adaptive baseline: its 990
queries compare with 999 for bisection, 1008 for the analytic proposal, 996 for ReLU

Evaluation contains 128 fresh states in each of dimensions two, four and eight.
Dimension four is absent from both training and calibration. All services receive
the identical states; three fresh-process repetitions preserve the complete timing
distribution. The saved coefficients and evaluation inputs also define the cross-
architecture replay. Repetitions and machine replay do not add independent states.
All streams are reproducible seeded numerical workloads. A seed alone is not an
assumption establishing population randomness; Proposition A.43 and the coverage
theorem state the separate assumptions needed for probabilistic extrapolation.
CP.2. Results and their economic interpretation
The two fitting attempts return finite coefficients without a recorded warning.
All held-out services meet the common certificate tolerance. The adaptive service
attains the smallest total query count in each evaluation dimension; at dimension
eight it ties bisection and the quadratic proposal. Its empirical query regret against
the declared menu is therefore zero in each dimension. This is not a zero expected-
regret theorem and not a comparison with the original Bellman optimum.
The ReLU proposal uses 987, 1017 and 987 queries in dimensions two, four and
eight, respectively, against 975, 993 and 969 for the adaptive service. The predictor
is genuinely shared and is evaluated on unseen states and an unseen dimension,
but it does not reduce verification work in this experiment. The protected first
partition already resolves many workloads before any model call. In the remaining
workloads, a model’s proposed query can fail to improve the protected baseline’s
allocation. All such calls and refinements are charged. This result identifies the
distinction between a valid common operator, a successfully returned fit and a
cost-saving proposal; none implies the next.
Complete process times include interpreter startup, coefficient loading, computa-
tion, serialization and shutdown. The numerical appendix reports every repetition
and peak resident memory on each recorded architecture, rather than only the
fastest execution. Logical dense-model arithmetic and disjoint oracle queries remain

APPENDIX CQ: DEPLOYMENT CHOICE UNDER QUALIFIED COST UNCERTAINTY
The attained continuation is an input to a complete economic decision, not merely
to another approximation score. The same qualified costs can support a choice
of acquisition precision across deployments. We retain the original NBO actors
and draw a controller before observing the initial state or innovations. This imple-
ments a mixture of complete policies, not an average of their actions, coefficients
or information sets. Its expected original-law cost is the corresponding mixture of
the qualified costs. Minimax-regret allocation has an established decision-theoretic
interpretation (Manski, 2004); the result below concerns the finite cost set supplied
by NBO qualification, conditional on its simultaneous coverage event.

APPENDIX CR: FROM RETURNED POLICIES TO ECONOMIC RESOURCE DECISIONS
An all-state upper bound and a comparison of actual policy costs answer different
economic questions. We now connect the policies returned by a construction frontier
to direct cost inference and then to a choice of implementation resources. The
construction data select the policies; independently generated evaluation paths
assess them. This separation permits a valid comparison of first-crossing policies
with different resolutions.
CR.1. Simultaneous inference after construction
Let H denote all construction information: primitive inputs, numerical labels,
fitted continuations, returned policies and complete certificate ladders. Conditional
on H, fix a finite catalogue of implemented-policy contrasts. Each implementation
includes its observation rule, original witness or nearest-node selector, true-state
feasible repair and action quantization. For a contrast i, let Di be the difference in
expected discounted costs under a specified initial law. A common-innovation path
score evaluates the two policies on their own endogenous trajectories. It is not the
difference between two regret bounds.
Suppose the initial and innovation uniforms are partitioned into equal bins.
Independent uniform bin indices are drawn, and interval simulation encloses the
score for every continuous realization inside the drawn bins. All unresolved state,
selector and repair branches remain in the enclosure. If [Ai, Bi] is a deterministic
support interval, clip the path endpoints to that support. Write mi, mi for outward
sample-mean bounds on the lower and upper endpoint samples and vi,L, vi,U for
upper bounds on their unbiased sample variances. For n ≥2 define

THEOREM A.61—Construction-conditional economic intervals: Under the stated
independent-bin model, conditional on any valid construction history H, with probability
at least 1 −α all catalogue contrasts satisfy
Di ∈[li, ui] := [max{Ai, mi −Ri(vi,L)},min{Bi, mi + Ri(vi,U)}].

The same coverage holds unconditionally. Subsequent selection among these covered con-
trasts, or evaluation at any deterministic implementation-price vector, needs no additional
union bound. This conclusion applies only to policies and initial laws included in the
catalogue; it does not create direct-cost observations for every unstudied tolerance or initial
state.
The proof is in Supplement, Section Q.10.
In particular, selecting the first policy to meet a specified certificate is permitted
when that selection uses construction records rather than the subsequent evaluation
paths. Repeated construction clocks are not independent draws from a neural-
optimizer population. The statistical randomness here belongs to the evaluation
design. A fixed pseudorandom stream implements a reproducible experiment; it is
not itself a proof of the independent-bin assumption.
CR.2. Replacement-fee identification
Write D = JW −JF. If witness is installed, replacing it by FVI changes total cost
by k −D, where k ≥0 is the replacement fee. If FVI is installed, the change is k + D.
Thus the two directional gains before fees are D and −D.
COROLLARY A.62—The break-even fee frontier: On an event where D ∈[l, u], the
two directional gains belong to [l, u] and [−u,−l]. The unknown absolute cost difference
satisfies
|D| ∈[dist(0,[l, u]),max{|l|,|u|}].
(A.144)
For every k ≥max{0, u,−l} neither replacement strictly lowers expected cost. By contrast,
k ≥max{0, l,−u} only removes a certified strictly profitable replacement. The two thresh-
olds generally differ. Strict inequalities in the first criterion certify that both replacements
strictly increase cost.

APPENDIX CS: CERTIFICATE-GATED NEURAL QUERIES
A prediction of the optimal action and a prediction of a useful numerical query are
different objects. Inserting a learned action before examining an already available
certificate charges an extra continuation query even when the two boundary actions
suffice. We instead make the demand for another query a mathematical decision and
let a trained NBO selector determine its location only after that demand has been
established. The underlying continuation recursion and the economic optimum are
unchanged.
At a recursive state, start with the two feasible action endpoints. Compute the
global lower bound from the parabolic minorants of Lemma A.73, including the
capacity remainder, and the smallest upper endpoint. Return immediately when

sumptions of Theorem A.74, the gated service returns the same original-optimum and
actual-policy guarantees for every supplied prediction, independently of fitting error. In

no predictor is evaluated at that state. If every prediction is declined at every recursive
query, the value endpoints and implemented actions coincide with those of the conventional
parabolic service using the same arithmetic and tie rules.
The proof is in Supplement, Section Q.8.
This theorem establishes robustness to the numerical content of a fitted prediction,
not that learning is free or always useful. It also does not state that an arbitrary
routed transcript has fewer queries than the adaptive conventional transcript. The
executed comparison records both possibilities. Unlike a policy catalogue with a
stored reference action at every state, neither service constructs a conventional state
lattice before it can return a certified policy.

depth-first scalar implementation can retain the current action partition and one
innovation child at a time. The executed batched implementation instead reports its
maximum state batch and process peak memory. A zero count of stored state-lattice
nodes does not mean zero storage.
The deterministic certificate is valid for any supplied finite network weights. A
failure to fit and return such weights is a separate service event. Our reliability esti-
mand is the return count and worst measured complete work over the preregistered
finite seed catalogue, with every repetition retained. Numerical workload paths
are not optimizer replications. The real-arithmetic cap and the exact-rational preci-
sion condition establish algorithmic termination at admissible tolerances; recorded
processor seconds are descriptive, not a hardware-uniform worst-case bound.

CS.2. An explicit economic purchase criterion
The decision maker buys a callable controller rather than a table of successful
sample decisions. Fix a physical capital numeraire for the normalized state, a
conversion m > 0 dollars per unit of the model’s loss index, a computation charge
p ≥0 dollars per measured second, and a fixed deployment fee f ≥0 dollars. For n
uses under a specified initial-state law, the monetary objective is
C(π) = nm E[Jπ
0 (X0)] + pW(π) + f.
These are declared preference and service-price parameters, not estimated economic
primitives. The policy theorem bounds the expected loss under the original continu-
ous law for every such initial-state law. The finite dyadic workload below measures
execution; its average cost is not substituted for that expectation.
If two policies have an independently valid expected-gain interval [l, u] for
E[Jπ0
0 −Jπ1
0 ], and their incremental measured service charge is ∆= p(W1 −W0) +
f1 −f0, then the monetary net gain lies in
[nml −∆, nmu −∆].
This follows by multiplication by the positive numeraire conversion and subtraction
of the same service charge. A positive lower endpoint supports purchase; a negative
upper endpoint rules it out at the stated prices. Uniform regret certificates alone do
not supply a directional expected-gain interval. They instead support a worst-case
accuracy requirement imposed before selecting the least expensive eligible service.
Finally, a forecast of amortized query work is distinguishable from a measured
complete service. With a fixed model and exactly repeated query workload, if
training requires B operations and deployment requires DL rather than DC oper-
ations per workload, then learning uses fewer total operations after k repetitions
precisely when DL < DC and k > B/(DC −DL). If DL ≥DC and B ≥0, no repeti-
tion of that unchanged workload produces an operation saving. This arithmetic
criterion includes training and cannot be applied to unrelated future states without
a new assumption. The executed catalogue reports its own full process clocks, not a
favorable hypothetical amortization.

APPENDIX CT: WHEN A PREDICTED QUERY COMPLETES THE CERTIFICATE
The safeguarded theorem is insensitive to the quality of a supplied prediction.
A separate question is when that prediction is sufficient to finish verification. The
answer must concern both the selected action and the unresolved lower bound.
Proximity to a minimizer alone does not make a coarse lower certificate accurate.
PROPOSITION A.65—Witness accuracy and certificate localization: Let f be a
differentiable, H-semiconcave objective with H ≥0 on [0, c], let a∗minimize f , and suppose
| f ′| ≤Λ. An evaluated proposal ba lies in [0, c], where 0 < c ≤c and c −c ≤∆. Each
endpoint interval is a valid enclosure of f and has width at most w. Suppose the partition
containing ba covers [0, c] and has maximum interval length h. Let L be its parabolic
lower certificate with the capacity allowance Λ∆, and let U be the smallest upper endpoint,
retaining earlier valid bounds as in the query algorithm. With e = |ba −a∗| and λ = | f ′(a∗)|,
U −L ≤2w + Λ∆+ Hh2
8
+ λe + He2
2 .
(A.148)
For an interior minimizer λ = 0. At a boundary the linear term cannot generally be removed.
Thus the right side at most δ is a sufficient certificate-return condition, not an assumption
that a trained prediction meets it.
If old and new valid endpoint records give (L,U) and (L′,U′) after one additional query,
with the running maximum lower bound and minimum upper bound, then
(U −L) −(U′ −L′) = (U −U′) + (L′ −L) ≥0.
(A.149)
An added prediction may have zero certified progress. The same identities apply to a conven-
tional query.
The proof is in Supplement, Section Q.9.
This proposition isolates what a fitted representation can contribute without cred-
iting it with a conventional solution. It can provide a small-error witness and change
which unresolved interval is refined. The global partition, endpoint arithmetic and
capacity account still have to support that witness. The maximum-width sufficient
condition is deliberately conservative; the implemented minimum-minorant rule
can stop earlier when only a subset of the partition remains competitive.

CT.1. A complete accuracy contract and its resource dependence
For T dates and target ϵ, write ST = ∑t<T βt. The recorded service chooses a
common local tolerance by rounding ϵ/(2ST) to binary64 and verifies the final
outward allowance. Under dGr ≤27, a uniform per-date acquisition allowance at
forty bits is
αb =

8 + 297β
16
+ 27

2−40.
The service certifies (δ + αb)ST ≤ϵ. Each descendant request is δ/(4β), rounded as
in the actual code and included in its outward endpoint guard. At the smallest re-
quest in the two- and three-date catalogues, the declared thirty-two-bit action quan-
tum satisfies the exact-recovery condition δr > 8Λr2−32. The supplement checks
this inequality with rationals for every horizon and target, rather than inferring it
from a successful workload.
For fixed remaining horizon and accuracy, the bounds on action endpoints and
scalar-innovation bins are independent of state dimension in this normalized econ-
omy. The factors dGr and dMr are bounded, while every transition and cost still
reads d coordinates. A width-wθ one-layer ReLU predictor has O(dwθ) parameters
and evaluation work; a dense quadratic on the same features has O(d2) terms. These
statements identify the absence of a (n + 1)d stored state table. They do not count
an arbitrary-precision rational operation as a unit-cost floating operation and do
not suppress the product of descendant query counts as horizon grows.
The two fitted implementations and their conventional controls therefore share
one original-optimum contract, but need not share a transcript, a returned policy
or a runtime. The completed experiments charge their distinct transcripts. A finite-
catalogue reliability statement concerns all specified seeds and repetitions, including
fitting warnings. It is not a population statement about optimizer success.

CU.2. An additional vector witness
In the two-control economy a trained, projected and downward-rounded pro-
posal can supply a new evaluated upper witness. Its insertion leaves the triangular
lower cover unchanged. The original corner endpoints remain in that cover.
PROPOSITION A.67—Optional vector witnesses: Suppose a triangular action cover
has a valid global lower bound L and feasible evaluated witnesses with upper bound U.
Adding any finite number of feasible, correctly evaluated witnesses and replacing U by
the minimum of all their upper bounds preserves containment of the original feasible
infimum. Every returned witness with U −L ≤δ has original Bellman regret at most δ.
The conclusion is independent of the training method and of whether an added witness is a
vertex of the lower cover.
Proof. See Supplement, Section EJ.2. The vector benchmark changes the trained
proposal or the choice of a triangle to refine, not the authority of the global lower
cover. Its training objective remains action-label loss.
APPENDIX CV: FROM VALIDATED READOUTS TO COMPLETE DEPLOYMENT
The fixed-feature construction and its optimization certificate identify an achieved
numerical object. The next issue is its use after training. Independent validation
need not imply that the states subsequently visited by a controller are independent.
We give a work account that keeps those two sources of information separate and
charges the descendants of a failed screen.

CV.2. Policy identity, declined reuse, and adoption
Cost inference can be combined with a deployment clock only after identifying the
controller whose cost was estimated. The release checks the complete readout arrays,
tolerance, acquisition precision, action rounding and original kernels. Consider a
service processing B blocks of m trajectories each. In D predetermined blocks it
declines an incompatible readout and uses the benchmark ν; otherwise it uses a
fixed π. Suppose each block has the same initial law and economic primitives, and
the decline schedule is independent of the trajectories. Let [l, u] be a simultaneous
interval for ∆= E[Jπ −Jν].
PROPOSITION A.69—Complete-service adoption region: Let Wπ,Wν be complete
work observations under the same boundary. If v ≥0 values one normalized expected-cost
unit, p ≥0 prices one work unit, and f ≥0 is the incremental installation fee, then the net
cost difference belongs to
[ vm(B −D)l + p(Wπ −Wν) + f, vm(B −D)u + p(Wπ −Wν) + f ]
(A.153)
on the original simultaneous event. The statement holds for every such price triple on that
event. With observed work saving S = Wν −Wπ > 0, strict adoption is supported whenever
pS > f + vm(B −D)u.

APPENDIX CW: TRAINING, REUSE, AND POLICY-COST PRECISION
The experiment links the constructive readout to the actual controlled economy.
It compares representation and training loss at a common information budget,
validates a frozen readout on independent contexts, measures a longer deployment
window, and evaluates the returned controllers at a prespecified policy-cost margin.
The original continuous laws, state-dependent investment capacity and Bellman
target are unchanged.
CW.1. Design and information balance
The scalar tasks are (d, T, ε) = (2,2,1/128) and (8,3,1/64), with twenty-four-
bit state acquisition and thirty-two-bit downward action rounding. Four fitted
proposals receive the same forty-eight training states, approximate action labels and
verified boundary endpoints per nonterminal date. The certificate-aware hat–ReLU
and degree-four Bernstein readouts have exactly 5d box-constrained coefficients
and the same objective, penalty and optimizer budget. An action-label readout on
the same hat features separates the objective from the representation. A quadratic
label fit retains its explicitly different parameter count. Adaptive parabolic search

The hat basis has an exact finite ReLU realization. It also has a conventional
piecewise-linear interpretation, so this comparison does not count two encodings of
that basis as independent algorithms. The Bernstein comparison holds the coefficient
count and purchased information fixed. All fitted proposals use the same final
certificate. Every returned certificate-aware iterate is quantized and receives an
exact rational value of the objective and box dual gap from Proposition A.77. The
achieved gap is reported rather than assuming that an optimizer’s success flag
proves optimality.
The protocol fixes two fitting seeds and four process repetitions. It contains
eighty cold comparisons, sixteen independent-validation services, fifty-six reuse
services, two paired-inference services and thirty-four vector services: 188 complete
processes. All returned. This is finite-catalogue evidence for the complete verifier,
not a population claim about fitting success. Four clock repetitions are not four new
training samples. The construction, receipts and original source freeze predate this
manuscript integration; the publication replay adds no scientific observations.
The complete cold-start results are reported in Supplement Table DC.I. At a fixed
purchased-information and coefficient budget, the hat–ReLU readouts close 48 and
50 of 256 small-task validation contexts for the two seeds, compared with 25 and
21 for Bernstein. The achieved exact box dual gaps are at most 10−7 across the
certificate-aware catalogue. This is a method-specific improvement in the declared
context screen, not a uniform complete-runtime advantage. All methods and both
tasks remain in the supplementary validation table.
Cold-start work remains an exacting comparison. In the two-state task the median
complete hat–ReLU process takes about 0.465 seconds, against 0.365 for adaptive
search. In the eight-state task the respective medians are about 1.618 and 0.666
seconds; both use 2,594 policy-query evaluations in the displayed workload. These
counts exclude separately reported training queries. Thus the certified objective
is now an executed arm, but its execution is not an identified complete-work
improvement. The recorded fitting, prediction and descendant counts locate the
cost rather than attributing every successful return to a successful predictor.

CW.2. Prospective validation and reuse
Each fitted readout is frozen before a new predictor-independent context stream
drawn uniformly from the sixteen-bit dyadic state grid is generated. There are 256
contexts per nonterminal date. The validation calculation executes the declared
complete-action mesh recovery whenever the pre-query screen fails. Its clipped loss
bounds the additional root queries on every recorded context. The supplementary
table gives the achieved loss, actual recovery queries, simultaneous validation
upper bound and descendant counts for every task, date, method and seed. These
6,144 method–context–date evaluations validate the stated context law and fallback;
they are not relabeled as independent on-policy recursive states.
Each reuse process trains and serializes once and then serves sixty-four predeter-
mined blocks of eight trajectories. At block index 16 it deliberately receives a stale
acquisition identifier and uses the adaptive benchmark. Loading, hashing, identity
validation, rejection, queries, cash-path enclosures, durable files and process shut-
down are included. A stable observed crossing must begin by block index 48 and
remain below the matched adaptive prefix through index 63. This requirement is
fixed before execution.
Three of the eight hat–ReLU processes in the two-state task satisfy that stable-
prefix criterion; four have smaller final complete times than their matched adaptive
process. The Bernstein and quadratic rules also exhibit small-task crossings. None
of the learned processes wins the eight-state reuse comparison. In the small task,
the adaptive complete times range from about 3.17 to 7.13 seconds, while hat–ReLU
ranges from about 3.32 to 5.07 seconds. Consequently, a favorable matched crossing
cannot be interpreted as uniform amortized superiority. The operation counts and
every unfavorable repetition remain in the record.
The deployment theorem states what additional context-law and descendant-cost
information would be sufficient for a prospective work bound. The experiment
does not substitute its identity check for a distributional drift bound. Likewise, the
sixty-four-block window is not extrapolated to an unobserved stopping horizon.

A complete-time win is relative to the adaptive process with the same repetition index. Stable means an

CW.3. A cost comparison at the declared precision
The central inference change is the Bellman-centered observation of Theorem A.86.
It estimates the actual expected cost difference by evaluating optimal advantages
along each actual policy trajectory. The conditional Bellman expectations are eval-
uated with a tighter tolerance and paid for separately. The estimator is not the
difference between two policy-loss upper bounds, and its realized observation is
not asserted equal to a same-shock cash-cost difference.
For each scalar task the protocol fixes 1,024 new common-path rows, forty-eight-
bit continuous bins and evaluation tolerance ε/32. The policies are adaptive search,
certificate-aware hat–ReLU, certificate-aware Bernstein, and the original R67 ReLU
controller at its pinned fitting seed. That historical controller is loaded unchanged.
The predeclared loss margin is 1/256, with numerical and sampling half-width
allocations of 1/512 each. No new row is added after inspecting a sign or a failed
comparison. There are twelve paired contrasts across the two tasks on one centered-
inference event with failure probability at most 0.01.

CW.4. Two controls and the economic service
The vector study compares simplicial search, largest-edge uniform refinement,
a trained two-output hat readout and a trained two-output quadratic proposal at
two state dimensions and horizons two and three. Both learned rules purchase the
same twelve teacher states per nonterminal date. Their training objective is action-
label loss, not the scalar convex certificate loss. All receive the same triangular
lower certificate and feasible rounding rule under two independent continuous
innovations. The horizon-four hat proposal transfers its three-date model and is
identified as a transfer, not as a four-date fitted model.
Supplement Table DC.II reports every two-control workload.
The vector records contain actual continuous-bin policy paths, complete clocks,
peak resident memory and descendant counts. Eight paths per ordinary service,
and one per horizon-four transfer service, are workload diagnostics rather than a
precision-designed population comparison. The experiment adds a trained vector
comparison, but it does not identify a vector expected-cost ranking or remove
continuation-tree growth. Derivative branch-and-bound is not an executed arm of
this catalogue.

CW.5. Earlier evidence and independent reconstruction
The original R67 catalogue remains a separate, unchanged companion, together
with all preceding adverse studies. It records 212 returns, no neural complete-reuse
winner, unresolved ordinary cost intervals, forty-eight neural fitting warnings and a
severe horizon-four vector expansion. Those observations are not overwritten by the
new loss, new inference rows or different reuse window. The previous accumulation-
aliasing counterexample and corrected execution also remain unchanged.
The new publication audit verifies every R69 receipt and stored-file identity,
recomputes the achieved rational training certificates, checks every validation loss
and executes independently written rational path calculations. A second interval
implementation uses exact full-bin state and cost bounds, not only representative
points, for unambiguous acquired paths. Its coverage and every diagnostic dis-
agreement are recorded explicitly. This provides independent reconstruction of the
sampled cash-path calculation and independent final inference arithmetic. It is not
represented as an independent generation of every optimal-advantage endpoint or
of the largest vector Bellman descendant tree.

Each row has 256 new contexts; seed suffix 1 or 2 denotes 6901 or 6902. The upper bound is inde-
pendently recomputed from an exact sample sum and an outward radius. It applies to the declared

The validation family contains twenty-four task–date–method–seed records with
256 contexts per record. The logarithm allowance twelve covers the stated finite fam-
ily by a union bound. Reusing a context stream across methods induces dependence
between estimators but does not invalidate that bound. The same stream is not
counted as additional independent information for each method. The deterministic
work inequality is checked on every context. The distributional upper endpoint is
recomputed from the exact sample sum, an eighty-digit square root with an explicit
expansion, and outward conversion to the printed numerical endpoint.
The full-action recovery mesh in this validation design has a declared root cap K.
Its actual descendant queries are separately recorded. These observations do not
validate a different adaptive fallback by definition. In Theorem A.68, a distributional
transfer allowance and a complete endpoint-work cap are additional premises. The
theorem therefore handles predictable choices and dependent contexts without
asserting that the recorded recursive state stream is independent.
APPENDIX CY: PRECISION AND THE CONTINUOUS-LAW ESTIMAND
The centered observation is the sum of optimal Bellman advantages along an
actual policy trajectory. Its expectation equals policy loss. Subtracting two such
observations cancels the common initial optimal value in expectation. It does not
cancel cash-flow risk path by path, and no empirical fitted value is substituted
for the optimal value. Each conditional Bellman evaluation uses its own tolerance,
action covering and continuous-innovation integration account, whose work is
charged to the inference service.
The twelve paired intervals form one finite family over the two declared scalar
tasks. With logarithm allowance twelve, 2 · 12exp(−12) < 0.01. For example, a ratio-
nal partial sum of the exponential series already proves exp(12) > 2400; no rounded
logarithm is needed for the coverage claim. The ordinary cash-cost estimator uses

The mean conditional-value and state-bin component widths are recorded before
intersecting with valid local regret ranges. The intersection can substantially reduce

The absence of sampled ambiguity is an observation, not a theorem excluding

APPENDIX CZ: INDEPENDENT FULL-BIN RECONSTRUCTION
The new independent implementation imports no NBO numerical kernel. It
uses exact rational intervals for the continuous initial and innovation bins, twenty-
four-bit acquired-state comparisons, true-state feasibility, stage costs, transitions
and terminal costs. It treats the two cumulative endpoints as separate immutable
rational numbers. In a transition coordinate, the deterministic function
f (u, v) = 1
16 + u
2 + v
8 + u(1 −v)
16
has derivatives 1/2 + (1 −v)/16 ≥0 and 1/8 −u/16 ≥0 on the state cube. Thus
evaluation at the lower–lower and upper–upper corners bounds its range without
invoking the production interval library. Quadratic costs use exact interval squares;
shortage uses the monotone positive-part map followed by an interval square. Both
shocks keep their original widths and marginal laws.
The implementation checks that its complete bin enclosure lies inside the archived
cash-cost enclosure. A second, independently written rational midpoint calculation
checks acquisition and cumulative cost at a represented point. The midpoint test
is not substituted for the full-bin test. Across 3,706 physical path archives there
are 38,722 recorded path rows; 736 distinct payloads contain 14,242 unique rows.
Repeated timing copies are hash-checked and compared, but their duplicate rational
evaluation is not counted again. The independent full-bin replay covers all 14,242
unique rows, with no unresolved branch in this executed catalogue.
A separate exact-sum and high-precision calculation checks every final centered
confidence interval from its stored advantage endpoints. This independently verifies
final inference arithmetic, not the generation of those optimal-advantage endpoints.
The regression suite compares primitive identities and small complete value prob-
lems with separate rational formulas. It does not independently regenerate the
largest multivariate Bellman descendant tree. The release states these different
coverage levels rather than assigning an undifferentiated independent-verification
label to the whole program.

CZ.1. Prediction portability and retained disagreements
An initial strict replay stopped because one Bernstein validation prediction was
not bitwise equal to a recomputed value. That failed attempt, its original audit
source and traceback are retained on their own branch and in the publication
inputs. The failure does not by itself identify an invalid Bellman bound. Nor does
a successful rerun on another processor prove the earlier numerical result bitwise
reproducible.
The current audit checks the saved actual action on its declared lattice and recom-
putes its strong-convexity chord with exact rational arithmetic. A discrepancy with
a recomputed readout is additionally checked against the declared action-rounding
and prediction allowances, not accepted by an arbitrary numerical closeness thresh-
old. The original scientific endpoints, actions, models and source freeze are un-
changed. Numerical parameter identity, callable-policy identity and successful
certificate verification are distinct statements.
In particular, equality of saved readout arrays is necessary but not sufficient for
transferring a cost estimate to an implementation on a different arithmetic runtime.
The complete-service purchase region assumes the same numerical callable policy or
an additional valid implementation-transfer bound. Matching processor metadata
or passing a finite replay is not silently promoted to an all-state policy-identity
theorem.

or previously paid qualification calculation. The process receipts cover the com-

The machine-readable table retains both boundaries, and the general price region
remains valid with the actual charged work and installation fee.
The multiplier 504 follows from sixty-four blocks of eight trajectories with one
predetermined fallback block. In that block the service uses the benchmark itself,
giving zero expected policy-cost difference. In the other blocks it uses the fixed
candidate. The cost interval can therefore be scaled by 504 under the policy-identity
premise of Proposition A.69. A positive work saving is an observed matched process
difference, not a confidence bound for future latency. The complete timing range also
records all unfavorable repetitions and does not authorize selection of a favorable
timing result as a population estimate.
The parent receipt includes child launch, imports, fitting or loading, all policy
and path calculations, serialization, child exit and log flushing. Parent receipt
bookkeeping belongs to the group clock. Training, inference and publication replay
have different boundaries and are not assigned zero cost when excluded from a
displayed sub-account. The machine record includes the permitted CPU, thread
counts, available frequency and governor data. Processor frequency was not locked
by the experiment. Fine timing differences consequently remain descriptive even
when operation counts reproduce exactly.
The original normalized investment units are retained. The loss margin is fixed by
the numerical protocol; the value of a loss unit, compute price and installation fee
are purchaser inputs. This produces a transparent conditional adoption region, not
an estimated monetary welfare result. Its noninferiority and equivalence statements
concern the actual expected-cost target and do not imply strict neural superiority.

ple. The broader NBO development remains available under its original diffusion,

Stored is the maximum number of retained witnesses. Stale counts discarded records at the declared
context invalidation. Fill and lookup are internal subclocks, not the complete process boundary. The
lookup account includes record-load validation. Repeated storage, hashing, output and shutdown are
additionally included in complete receipts.
DD.1. Complete timing and retained records
The process receipt includes creation, Python imports, original Bellman fills, all
recursive descendants, cache retrieval, rational checks, repeated serialization, final
output and process exit. The driver writes a separate receipt after that boundary.
Summing child block clocks is not the complete process time. Every block’s body
prefix excludes imports and has its own exact definition in the source. The complete
receipts, rather than those prefixes, determine the reported timing comparison.

No processor frequency lock is claimed. The start and end records include the
selected CPU, frequency fields where the environment exposes them, interpreter
version and platform. A cyclic mode order limits a simple fixed-order confound
but does not create randomized hardware-frequency inference. Close clock differ-
ences require more evidence than the prescribed finite repetitions. Bellman action
counts are consequently reported separately from seconds. They are invariant de-
scriptive counts for these transcripts, not predictions of another implementation’s
throughput.
The 128-record cap bounds logical retained witnesses. It does not bound total
process resident memory: a fresh recursive fill can retain batched descendants,
interpreter state, interval work arrays and output buffers. The largest process
memory remains in the table. The executed cache operates at workload roots only.
The four-date pressure is not hidden by counting a later root hit as though the first
fill used no descendants.
DD.2. Independent checks and trusted premises
The additional admission audit matches all 708 returns to the prescribed state,
control dimension, horizon, tolerance and context epoch. Cache reloads in this
catalogue use the same process and numerical model. Arbitrarily supplied external
intervals are not made valid by deserialization or a file hash.
For a returned hit, the independent checker locates the earlier paid source record
with the same context, horizon, source state, action and endpoints. It recomputes
the original regularity constants, state distance, action displacement and interval
expansion in exact rational arithmetic. It checks the returned action’s lattice and
capacity and that the serialized binary endpoints contain the exact expanded in-
terval. A narrow stored interval alone would not prove that a source fill encloses
the original value: the inherited verifier and its primitive proof remain explicit
premises.
For conditional ReLU integration, the second implementation reconstructs the
original projected drift and shocks independently. It does not call the divided-power
formula. It clips the support rectangle against the affine neuron’s positive half-plane

DD.3. Development probe and publication preservation
Before the new source commitment, a vector development probe queried (0.4,0.6)
at tolerance 0.04 and horizons two, three and four. The first two returned. The probe
was stopped at its 35-second process limit while computing horizon four. Its log is
retained separately and is not merged with the later 900-second scientific catalogue
or used as a favorable timing observation.
Every R70 active section is assigned to exactly one current document and checked
byte for byte. All inherited formal statements and proofs are thereby retained,
not reconstructed from a favorable summary. The complete old main article and
supplement remain companion PDFs. New tables are derived from the committed
receipts and independent audit, and all four current documents are rebuilt from a
clean source directory. Visual inspection is documented against the exact PDF hashes
actually inspected. Compilation and tests do not constitute external mathematical
acceptance.

controller. The primal and dual calculations are exact rational checks, independently reconstructed
without relying on the optimizer status.
The ReLU basis consists of the constant and, in each coordinate, the identity and
positive parts at 1/4, 1/2 and 3/4. The conventional basis consists of the constant
and the four nonconstant degree-four Bernstein polynomials per coordinate. Their
valid feature moduli are respectively one and four. Having the same number of
coefficients does not make their function classes or approximation moduli identical.

rule; the label-loss ablation within each stage shares those exact labels and features.

checked with rational probability multipliers. The table’s gap is the achieved pri-
mal value minus the exact dual lower bound, not the solver’s reported duality
tolerance. Constant recentering changes the continuation gauge without changing
this objective. The predeclared success tolerance is 1/65536. The stored status and

qualification, matched least-squares ablations and the service output; the independent checker has a

its whole-cell gap. Thus the newly computed residual account is tied to original
primitives rather than only to a stored hash.

APPENDIX DF: EXACT SEQUENTIAL-LEDGER REGRESSIONS
The new regression suite checks conditional means, range reservation, target
changes and failed numerical episodes. Its adaptive binary-tree diagnostic enumer-
ates all 212 = 4096 leaves and every prefix, with exact probabilities and changing
predictable ranges. The event count is a finite-model check of the implemented
boundary, not an empirical substitute for the supermartingale proof. Rational loga-
rithm bounds and coefficient duals are also tested independently of floating solver
stopping flags.
A support failure and a numerical failure are deliberately different branches.
An empty intersection or a changed fixed target is rejected. A numerical failure
records the prequalified full support, advances the prefix and charges its work. The
interface cannot prove that a caller fixed the support before observing the episode;
that temporal and probabilistic premise remains part of the algorithm’s contract. A
cache carried across episodes is included in the target definition or is handled as
varying conditional cost.
All prior scientific arrays and sources remain unchanged. The ordinary-source
build runs the inherited and current tests and recomputes the published tables.
The clean archive includes the transitive R62 input sources, including the original
service kernel omitted by the interrupted R72 archive. The reproduction report
identifies the suites run inside that archive and compares actual PDF text and
page counts after deleting generated PDFs and tables. Visual inspection is recorded
separately against the output hashes. None of those publication checks is an external
mathematical acceptance decision.

APPENDIX DG: TRANSPORTING PURCHASED BELLMAN WITNESSES
A second way to control the descendant cost is to reuse a calculation already
purchased. Exact memoization only recognizes the same state. The following rule
transfers a lower Bellman bound and its feasible upper witness to a nearby state,
after repairing capacity and accounting for the full displacement. It is compatible
with either a neural or a conventional generator of the original certified record.

of the inequalities is a separate premise. For the original scalar and two-control
economies, let

THEOREM A.70—Reuse after capacity repair: Under the stated record and modulus
conditions,
L(x) ≤V∗
r (x) ≤Q∗
r (x,ea) ≤U(x).
Hence outward endpoints with U(x) −L(x) ≤δ permit the actual repaired action to be
returned without a new Bellman query. An identity mismatch, failed feasibility check or
excessive width requires a new verified calculation; proximity alone licenses no reuse.
The same assertion holds after any history-dependent selection of valid records. At each
future date, suppose the selected record or fresh query supplies the original local-gap and
acquisition premises of Theorem A.74. The resulting, possibly history-dependent controller
retains that theorem’s original-optimum loss sum. It need not coincide with the action
returned by a fresh search at the same tolerance.
The proof is in Supplement, Section EK.3.
The implemented repair first rounds the new capacity downward on the 2−32
lattice, scales a vector action proportionally when necessary, and rounds each
coordinate downward. The certificate charges its exact resulting ℓ1 displacement,
not merely the change in capacity. Retrieval may use approximate distances or a
learned index as an ordering heuristic. Every returned hit must still satisfy (A.154)
under outward arithmetic.

This bound makes the dimensional price of uniform reuse explicit. It is not a
dimension-free caching theorem. It also separates a first expensive Bellman fill from
later transport checks. Caching at the workload root can avoid all descendants on
a hit, but does not accelerate the descendants of a miss. The executed bounded
cache uses 128 records and the requested fill tolerance, not the tighter γδ premise.
Its operation counts below are direct observations, not an application of (A.156). A
cache at recursive descendants would need a separate execution and ledger.
APPENDIX DH: CONTINUATION EVALUATION AND PAID QUERY REUSE
The evidence separates three questions: whether a certified readout returns an
admissible policy, whether its actual expected cost meets a declared margin, and
whether a purchased calculation can be reused profitably. The preceding training
and inference catalogue remains unchanged. The new execution fixes localized
query workloads and exact conditional-moment checks before running them. It
changes neither the economic primitives nor the continuous feasible-action target.

DH.1. Retained trained policies and economic precision
The retained 188-process catalogue is reproduced in Appendix, Section CW.
Hat–ReLU and Bernstein readouts purchase the same teacher information and
have exactly 5d coefficients; the achieved objective and box dual gaps are recom-
puted rationally. Independent validation and sixty-four-block reuse receive separate
work accounts. Both their favorable and unfavorable repetitions remain visible. In
particular, the eight-state task does not identify a learned complete-work winner.
The direct policy-cost experiment fixes its sample count and numerical pre-
cision before execution. All twelve original-law paired intervals lie within the
declared equivalence region [−1/256,1/256], and all contain zero. The two
adaptive-minus-hat–ReLU intervals are approximately [−0.00068263,0.00070764]
and [−0.00160291,0.00160253]. Their shared inference services cost about 9.03 and
408.63 seconds. These are informative quality comparisons with expensive qualifi-
cation, not an identified neural cost ranking or a free inference improvement. The
complete precision and adoption tables are retained in the appendix.
The frozen-continuation theorem supplies a different way to evaluate that
expected-cost estimand. Its moment component is executed here; a new trained
critic meeting the old equivalence margin at lower complete qualification cost is
not presumed. The earlier optimal-advantage observations are not counted again
as samples of the new formula.
DH.2. A fixed original-law query catalogue
The new design has five tasks: two scalar-control tasks at (d, T) = (2,2),(8,3)
and three two-control tasks at (d, T) = (2,2),(2,3),(2,4). Each task has three rules:
fresh calculation, exact-key reuse and geometric witness transport. The source
commitment fixes the task list, tolerances, repetition counts, 128-record capacity,
invalidation schedule, workload order and 900-second per-process limit. There are
36 prescribed complete processes. None trains a new action predictor or loads a
precomputed conventional policy.
A workload starts at alternating coordinates 0.4,0.6. Odd requests repeat that
state. Predetermined even requests perturb one coordinate by 2−20. Except in the

four-date stress case, a late distant request has every coordinate equal to 0.75, and a
specified earlier block invalidates the context. The first four tasks have 32, 16, 24
and 8 requests; the four-date task has four. The first three tasks have three timing
repetitions, the three-date vector task two, and the four-date task one. Rules are
executed in a fixed cyclic order across repetitions.
Every miss calls the unchanged original recursive verifier at the declared toler-
ance. Every hit uses the exact state-transfer and capacity-repair test. The cache is
serialized, hashed, reloaded and validated after every block. The receipt begins
before process creation and ends after exit, including imports, all descendant work,
file output and shutdown; writing the parent receipt itself is separate publication
overhead. A single CPU is pinned. Available start and end frequency information is
recorded, but frequency is not locked. Repetitions support descriptive comparisons,
not a hardware-uniform or population timing theorem.
The table counts Bellman action evaluations at all descendants, not only workload
roots. Geometric hits at a nonidentical state distinguish transport from exact memo-
ization. Their capacity-repair count is separately recorded, including downward
repairs that change the returned action. The distant request and context invalidation
test whether a cheaper rule refuses an unjustified reuse rather than forcing a hit. An
unchanged numerical law with a new context identifier still triggers the declared
conservative invalidation.
The four-date task retains the first expensive tree. A hit avoids that tree on
a later request, whereas a miss pays for it again. This is a local repeated-query
improvement under the original optimum contract, not a disappearance of the long-
horizon first-fill cost. The trace records every source witness, state displacement,
repaired action and outward endpoint. The absence of a state lattice does not justify
omitting either the descendant count or resident memory.
The full repetition and storage ledger is in Appendix, Section DD. Prefix clocks
there begin after module loading and are labeled as body clocks; they are not
substituted for complete process receipts. The bounded cache and requested fill
tolerance do not satisfy the stronger retained-cover premises of Proposition A.71,
so that proposition’s uniform packing count is not presented as an empirical result.

DH.3. Independent conditional-moment and transport checks
The rational integration catalogue uses four (d, m) specifications, namely
(2,1),(8,1),(2,2),(8,2), and 64 state–action contexts per specification. Each context
has sixteen rational neurons. The original bilinear state drift, action exposure and
uniform innovation projections are evaluated exactly. An independent checker
clips the corresponding innovation rectangle and integrates the affine neuron
through polygon area and first moments. It imports no production moment, cache
or interval-query routine.

DH.4. Constructed continuations and attained qualification
The readout theorem is executed in four predeclared backward constructions in
the original two-state, two-date, scalar-control economy. Two midpoint covers, with
eight or sixteen cells per coordinate, are crossed with additive shallow ReLU and
degree-four Bernstein features. Each basis has nine coefficients bounded by eight.
At each date the future is the continuation actually constructed at the next date.
Exact conditional moments supply thirty-three continuous feasible action values per
node and thirty-three robust, downward-quantized acquired-action proposals. The
original state-dependent capacity and continuous innovation law are unchanged.
