Every new action value is independently reconstructed using the retained origi-
nal rational terminal formula or a different exact integration method for the fitted
continuation. Continuous-action lower covers, whole-cell choices and primal–dual
bounds are then recomputed. These constructions add actual qualified continua-
tions, not new independent cost observations. The stopping theorem has separate
exact finite-model regressions; the earlier fixed-sample equivalence intervals are
not retroactively given an anytime interpretation.
APPENDIX DI: COMPLETE CONSTRUCTED-POLICY COST RECORDS
This appendix reports the entire prospectively specified cost catalogue. The poli-
cies are the four acquired actors already returned by the qualification-optimal
backward constructions, together with zero investment. The constant action on
a cell is read from the original integer action array. No proposed readout is re-
trained on these paths, and no callback to the optimal Bellman recursion replaces its
actual fitted future. At a fixed acquisition resolution, the ReLU and Bernstein con-
structions have the same nine-coefficient budget and state-and-action information.
Cross-resolution comparisons answer a different question and retain their distinct
observation contracts.

Width and Equiv. are exact-endpoint decisions at the separate predeclared thresholds, each 1/256. Posi-
tive zero-minus-controller means a gain from replacing the zero incumbent. Common-path dependence
is retained; the twenty intervals are not twenty independent samples.
The width and equivalence columns are different decisions. A precisely positive
gain over the installed zero-investment controller fails equivalence because it iden-
tifies a material improvement, not because its computation failed. Conversely, a
small point estimate with an interval spanning the chosen margin cannot justify
equivalence. All decisions use unrounded rational endpoints. The printed inter-
vals are rounded outwards, so a reader need not infer a sign from a decimal that
understates uncertainty.
DI.1. Acquisition, bin integration and arithmetic
Each path row contains two initial-state and two innovation bin indices. A forty-
bit bin represents its full original-law continuous cell. The implementation does not
replace the conditional distribution within the bin by a midpoint. At each date, a
rectangle enclosing the true state can intersect several acquired cells. The selected
action range then includes every cell in that rectangle. Closed upper boundaries
are included conservatively. The endpoint calculation propagates that entire range
through the stage cost and next transition.

Unrounded components sum exactly to the recorded width. The numerical term is the mean retained full-
bin endpoint width, including acquisition and arithmetic effects; these are not asserted to be separately
additive causes. Variance terms use exact endpoint sample variances and upward rational square roots.
The first evaluator uses centered polynomial expressions with binary64 outward
operations. The second expands the cost and transition polynomials and uses inte-
ger floor and ceiling on a 2−48 grid. It obtains acquired-action extrema by directly
enumerating each distinct intersected rectangle rather than reading the first evalua-
tor’s range tables. Thus it shares neither floating arithmetic nor cost, transition or
lookup routines with the production evaluator. The stored endpoints use the hull,
not the more optimistic intersection, of these two evaluations. Intersection with the
global primitive support is justified separately.
Every new full-bin path is recomputed by both implementations during replay.
A further exact-rational midpoint calculation checks 512 predetermined rows for
each policy, including both estimators. Synthetic boundary tests exercise bins at the
state and innovation extremes and across acquired-cell boundaries. These point-
wise tests supplement the interval-propagation proof; they are not called full-bin
verification by themselves. The historical aliasing counterexample and its corrected
R67 execution remain unchanged.
DI.2. Statistical allocation
There are 30 estimands and 60 one-sided endpoint events in one fixed family. The
empirical-Bernstein radii use the common log allowance ten. The union bound is at
most 120e−10 < 1/100, verified independently by a rational lower partial sum for
e10. All endpoint sums and sums of squares are integer calculations, so no floating
sample-variance cancellation enters the confidence endpoints. Upward rational
square roots enlarge rather than shrink the radii.
The new family is distinct from the earlier R69 optimal-advantage-centered
inference family. Combining conclusions from different families requires adding
their error allowances. The R73 construction records contain no new independent
cost rows, and replay of the R77 rows adds none. The sample stream, row count,
bin precision, policy hashes, estimands and margin are fixed before execution. A

Corollary A.59 provides a priced decision for every declared deployment count
and monetary scale. In particular, the gain interval in Table CL.I yields an entire
replacement-fee frontier, rather than a favorable isolated fee. The zero-investment
incumbent is a feasible installed policy in the original economy. An improvement
over it does not establish dominance over an adaptive Bellman search or over every
conventional basis. The matched feature comparison and the retained conventional-
query catalogue must be read separately.
The experiment’s units are those of the theoretical investment loss. A currency
calibration, an empirically estimated installation fee and a deployment-frequency
model would be additional economic assumptions. The mathematical adoption
interval states their role explicitly and remains valid for all such nonnegative prices
on the same coverage event. It therefore supports a conditional purchase calculation
without manufacturing an empirical welfare estimate.
APPENDIX DJ: SIMULTANEOUS CHOICE AMONG CONSTRUCTED CONTROLLERS
The preceding experiment qualifies the same complete controllers returned by

costs give the valid rule in Corollary A.59, but discard the more precise paired
observations. We retain all available comparisons on their original simultaneous
event. No additional simulation, independence assumption between estimators, or
allocation of statistical error is required.

Let [l, u] be the closed interval for JReLU,8 −JReLU,16. Suppose only the finer con-

mately 0.00070894. Exact endpoints, all adjacent gaps and attaining cost vectors
are deposited. Transitive closure does not further tighten the paired bounds in this
particular catalogue; no such improvement is claimed.

total charge divided by mv. This gives a complete conditional fee region without
assigning a monetary value to normalized losses or inferring a deployment horizon
from the sample count. Acquiring finer information is an economic choice only after
its actual incremental costs are specified.

DK.1. Refinement charges and the finite comparison
Let the fine and coarse ReLU controllers be denoted by A and B, with JB −JA ∈
[l, u], where these endpoints are the tight implications of C. Suppose all policies
except A have a common charge and A has an additional charge f . The retained
inequalities identify B as less costly than every other controller in the catalogue, so
those controllers cannot be a best-cost comparator or a regret-minimizing choice.
Equation (A.159) reduces to
ΓA( f ) = max{0, f −l},
ΓB( f ) = max{0, u −f }.
For f ≤l, only A can have positive strict cost advantages against all alternatives;
its worst-case regret is zero. For f ≥u, B has zero worst-case regret. On [l, u],
the difference of the two regrets is 2f −l −u, proving the switching formula. At a
boundary, universal weak optimality, rather than strict optimality, is the appropriate
statement. The independently checked exact fee probes include both boundaries,
the switching point, and points outside the ambiguity interval.

the investment economy.

DL.1. Installed subsets rather than free simultaneous availability
Suppose a decision maker serves m ≥1 deployments and may install a nonempty
subset S at total normalized cost K(S). Write Ki = K({i}), and assume K(S) ≥Ki
for every i ∈S. The benchmark installs the best single controller, paying its own Kj.
For p supported on S, the exact worst-case average regret is
RS(p, w) = max
j
(
∑
i
piHji(w) + K(S) −Kj
m
)
.
(A.160)
Indeed, the installation term is independent of θ, and the same attaining potential
proves the formula. The assumption on K makes the cost of an allocation at least
the weighted average of its corresponding singleton costs, and hence at least their
minimum; the regret is nonnegative. For each subset, (A.160) is a linear program
on ∆S. Enumerating the nonempty subsets and retaining the least optimum yields
the exact installation-and-allocation decision. It requires at most 2q −1 programs
and is not advertised as dimension-free optimization. Lower bounds from the dual
of every subset, together with an attaining primal allocation for the chosen subset,
certify a global solution. A controller outside the installed subset remains a possible
oracle comparator and must not be removed from the rows.
DL.2. Two-controller formula and extra setup threshold
With only the fine controller charged f , put a = f −l and b = u −f . Within the
ambiguity region both are positive and a + b = u −l. If p is the fine share, the two
worst-case comparator regrets are pa and (1 −p)b. Their maximum is minimized at
their intersection, giving p = b/(a + b) and value ab/(a + b). Outside that region
a uniformly optimal pure controller has zero regret. If l = u, the gain is known
exactly: use the fine controller below l, the coarse one above it, and any allocation
at equality; no division by a zero width is needed.
When both controllers incur additional cost κ only for 0 < p < 1, their optimal
nontrivial allocation is unchanged and its value is ab/(a + b) + κ. The best pure

DL.3. A deterministic allocation to a finite cohort
Random assignment is unnecessary when m homogeneous deployments with
the same expected cost law can be assigned in advance. Deploy A on exactly k
tasks and B on the others, without choosing tasks according to unqualified outcome
information. The average expected cost is the mixture with p = k/m; independence
between tasks is not needed for this expectation identity. For l < f < u, a minimizing
integer k is one of ⌊mp∗

An extra two-controller setup charge is included only for 0 < k < m; both pure
endpoints must then also be tested. Nonhomogeneous deployment laws require
separately qualified cost vectors and are not covered by relabeling the existing
sample as a cohort.
The deposited implementation checks exact probability feasibility, all original cost
inequalities at each attaining potential, and equality between primal and dual pay-
offs. Two-policy formulas are checked against a separate exhaustive rational vertex
solver on the full five-controller catalogue. Finite-cohort choices are checked against
every integer allocation. The original thirty cost estimands, 524,288 evaluation rows,
fitted coefficients, scientific clocks and adverse selector comparisons remain un-
changed. The optimization tables contain no new simulation or timing evidence.
The sharpness claim is relative to the retained interval system; neither an exact
decision solution nor a positive finite comparison establishes a population-wide
neural ranking.

APPENDIX DM: NEURAL BELLMAN QUERIES WITHOUT A STATE LATTICE
The preceding construction makes numerical error accountable, but a complete
tensor reference can absorb the benefit of a fitted continuation. We therefore change
the computational organization, not the economic problem. A Neural Bellman
selector proposes an action at the state actually acquired. A recursive interval query
then bounds the original Bellman value at that state and checks the proposed
action against the entire continuous feasible interval. No conventional policy is
precomputed at all states. The controller is the resulting callable algorithm, not the
unverified proposal alone.
The distinction matters for attribution. Learning may reduce the work needed
to locate a useful action. It does not supply the inequalities used to certify that
action. The adaptive conventional comparator receives the same inequalities and
the same original-optimum target. The trained value-fit policies in the preceding
study remain distinct from the action-query predictor introduced here.

At an acquired state, retain an ordered partition of the feasible action interval and

upper bound is the minimum over every evaluated feasible witness.

The finite-precision contract is explicit. The executed service uses the width guard,
a 512-point cap, and a 32-bit downward action lattice. A precision or cap failure
withholds the floating certificate and invokes a separately counted exact-rational
enumeration. This fallback constructs values only at the required descendants; it
does not load a precomputed conventional policy. The rational fallback chooses
dyadic action and quadrature counts until each cover or quadrature allowance is
at most one quarter of the request, and requests child width at most one quarter
divided by the discount. Provided δ > 8Λr2−32 at every recursive level, its exact
brackets have width at most three quarters of the request. This proves a finite
return for every acquired state in the declared tasks, including states absent from
the workload. Rational bit-operation cost is additional work and is not replaced
by a unit-cost floating clock. The mathematical point budget is checked against
the declared tolerance range; termination in an arbitrary floating implementation
is not inferred merely from the real-arithmetic argument. Fitting convergence is
unnecessary for validity: any finite prediction, and even its clipped replacement
when numerically invalid, is only a proposed query.

The constants dGr, dMr are bounded independently of d, so the declared endpoint
and quadrature budgets need not grow exponentially with the state dimension.
Primitive evaluations still cost O(d). This removes the state lattice, not the hori-
zon or shock-tree cost. The executed vectorization batches a query’s innovation
descendants. Its largest live state batch is reported; it does not claim the smaller
memory of a fully streamed implementation. Increasing the horizon or the shock di-
mension may still be expensive. The new execution is scalar-control; the earlier full
two-control result is retained rather than relabeled as a query-service experiment.
A useful prediction can reduce the endpoint count or return its own action
from the initial partition. An inaccurate prediction can instead add work. This is a
prediction-dependent algorithm, not a theorem of neural dominance. Learned warm
starts have their own literature, including Sakaue and Oki (2023); their discrete-
convex setting differs from the original-law Bellman intervals here. Convex control
policies and learned optimization parameters are studied by Agrawal et al. (2020).
Our comparison identifies the extra proposal cost and the resulting query transcript
rather than claiming priority for learning a warm start.
The purchase is now a complete callable controller with a declared error contract.
Its training cost, every subsequent certified query, and its return-time cost belong to
the same service. A reduction in queried state storage is economically relevant for
repeated decisions only after these costs are counted. The original cost normalization
is maintained. Workload seconds and normalized expected-cost loss are reported
separately; a price per unit of computation can convert the former to the latter only
as an explicitly specified decision-maker parameter.

THEOREM A.78—Simplicial Bellman query: For the two-control primitives, (A.173)
is a lower minorant of the true Bellman objective. Taking the smallest valid triangle lower
endpoint and the best feasible-action upper endpoint gives a lower–upper certificate for
the full continuous simplex. Include the omitted capacity strip and actual action-rounding
allowances. Returning when this gap is at most δ gives the same acquired-policy loss
recursion as Theorem A.74.
A failed floating triangulation can be replaced by an exact-rational simplex enumeration.
Under the stated positive precision slack, this recovery is finite at every finite horizon. With
two innovations divided into q bins each, a valid local quadrature error is

PROPOSITION A.79—First-disagreement cost bound: If bπ is the reference policy
and Dt is the event that the coupled policies first choose different actions at date t, then
|Jπ −J bπ| ≤
T−1
∑
t=0
btHt Pr(Dt) ≤
T−1
∑
t=0
btHt Pr

(A.177)
The first events are disjoint. Any independent bound on the entire cash-cost difference may
be intersected with this bound. To apply it to an optimization class, the action agreement
and bad sets must hold uniformly for every policy in that class.
PROOF:
On Dt, the histories, states and costs before t coincide. The absolute
difference of the remaining discounted costs is at most btHt. On the event of
no disagreement the costs coincide throughout. Summing over the disjoint first-
disagreement events and taking expectations proves the first inequality. Up to the
first disagreement, the common state is the state of the reference policy driven by
the same innovations. A first disagreement at date t requires this state to lie in Et,
proving the second inequality.
Q.E.D.
This proposition is a cost-transfer identity, not a substitute for constructing longer-
horizon stable sublevels. In particular, changing a terminal readout changes labels
upstream. Independently small optimization gaps at different fitted label prob-
lems do not automatically establish the uniform action-agreement premise. In the
executed two-date experiment the last-date actor depends only on the common
terminal payoff; Theorem A.49 therefore needs the first-date switch problems alone.
DP.3. Confidence and economic interpretation
The original cost event concerns a finite list of frozen attained policies. On that
event all deterministic stability enlargements are valid simultaneously, including
for a coefficient vector selected after seeing the records but still belonging to a
certified fixed-label sublevel. The probability statement does not change because

A failed action-stability certificate is a numerical statement about the available
lower bound, not a witness of policy variation. Conversely, policy invariance of
an exact optimization class does not assert that an arbitrary practical optimizer
reaches that class. The deposited feasible iterate and dual gap describe what the
construction attained; the switch lower bounds describe what every member of a
stated sublevel must do. These are distinct quantifiers, and neither is inferred from
a collection of fitting seeds.
For the two calibrated n = 16 controllers let [l, u] be the positive interval for
ReLU cost minus Bernstein cost. Let κ be the additional per-deployment charge for
Bernstein, after all actual installation and computation charges have been converted
into the same normalized cost units. The corresponding net difference is [l −κ, u −κ].
Bernstein is strictly less costly for every κ < l; ReLU is strictly less costly for every
κ > u; neither strict ordering is certified in the intermediate region. This is an exact
conditional price region, not a monetary calibration. It remains valid for the fully
action-stable optimizer classes, and it does not use construction times with different
service boundaries as interchangeable monetary prices.

APPENDIX DR: ACTIONWISE ECONOMIC TRANSFER AND ITS COMPLETE
NUMERICAL ACCOUNT
Theorem A.50 separates two numerical tasks. The action-switch dual identifies
actions that cannot be selected by a qualified readout. Original-law integration
prices the actions not excluded by that dual. Neither calculation substitutes a fitted
critic for the cost of the implemented continuation policy.
DR.1. Conditional contrasts from the original primitives
For a fixed initial cell C, reference action a, and alternative action b, couple
the two trajectories with the same first innovation W. Write Yb,Ya for their next
states and B = τ1(Yb), A = τ1(Ya) for the fixed last-date actor. The action pair need
not agree on the two next states. Let m(y, d) denote the original transition with
innovation zero and action d. Its opposite-signed last innovation leaves the state
sum unchanged, so the shortage term in the terminal cost is unaffected. The terminal
quadratic terms give
E[g(m(y, d) + (W′,−W′)) | y, d] = g(m(y, d)) + 5E[(W′)2] = g(m(y, d)) +
5
3072.
(A.178)
The correction is the same for both trajectories and cancels in their difference. It
cannot be omitted from an individual conditional cost. Feasibility and the inherited
transition bounds ensure that the actual states remain in [0,1]2; intersecting an
enclosing box with this domain does not clip the economic transition law.

PROPOSITION A.80—Complete-bin enclosure: Partition each initial cell into r2
equal rectangles and the first innovation into q equal bins, with dyadic r, q. Evaluate
(A.179) on every complete subbox by outward interval operations. On each next-state
rectangle, enclose the fixed actor by the minimum and maximum of its action indices over
every intersected acquired cell, including boundary cells. Let [ls, us] be the resulting paired
interval on subbox s, intersected with the valid signed support [−H, H]. Then

PROOF: The transition and centered identities are algebraic identities for every
state and innovation in the subbox. The rectangle extrema contain the actual actor
action even when the rectangle crosses an actor discontinuity. Interval inclusion,
propagated through each arithmetic operation and the valid intersections, therefore
contains (A.179) pointwise. Equation (A.178) accounts for the remaining innovation
under its actual continuous marginal law. All subboxes have exact conditional
probability 1/(r2q), so integration preserves the endpoint inequalities. Taking a
hull preserves inclusion, as does intersecting two bands that separately contain the
same integral.
Q.E.D.
The two deposited implementations do not import each other’s interval, transi-
tion, cost, partition or actor routines. The binary64 implementation uses outward
next-representable-number operations and a precomputed rectangle-extremum
table. The integer implementation uses Python-integer endpoints in units 2−48,
directed integer division, expanded cost polynomials and direct enumeration of
distinct acquisition rectangles. Their endpoint streams must overlap on every sub-
box. A separately written rational trajectory calculation checks four deterministic
midpoint trajectories per action and rung. Those checks are regressions; the proof
concerns every point in each box, not only its midpoint.
The complete records retain exact integer endpoint sums, their common denomi-
nator, the digest of all four independently computed endpoint streams, the largest
endpoint discrepancy and the number of processed boxes. They do not claim to
deposit an additional random sample or to count the two arithmetic implementa-
tions as independent statistical observations. Full replay recomputes those endpoint
streams, not only the saved sums.
DR.2. Refinement and resource requirements

pair. In exact interval arithmetic, the integrated width in Proposition A.80 tends to zero
as r, q →∞along dyadic partitions. The same conclusion holds with outward arithmetic

If P alternatives remain at the largest qualification tolerance, a level uses exactly Pr2q
paired subboxes in each implementation. Its binary64 actor tables occupy O(n4) entries and
the direct preprocessing used here takes at most O(n6) operations. After that preprocessing
each rectangle query is constant work. The independent enumerator instead stores the n2
actor indices, groups queried rectangles by sorting their codes, and can inspect up to n2
indices per distinct rectangle. Its conservative worst-case work is therefore

Pr2q [n2 + log(r2q)]

.
Processing one alternative at a time uses O(n4 + r2q) numerical working storage, apart
from retained integrated records.
PROOF:
For a fixed first action, each next-state coordinate is a polynomial of
the initial state plus either W or −W. For any terminal acquisition boundary Yj =
k/n, its preimage has conditional innovation measure zero for every initial state,
because the coefficient of W is nonzero. There are finitely many boundaries and two
coupled trajectories. Fubini’s theorem therefore gives a measure-zero union of their
preimages in the integration domain.
At every other interior point, sufficiently fine boxes intersect only the fixed actor
cell containing each next state. On such boxes, (A.179) is a finite composition of
continuous polynomial and positive-part operations with constant actor actions.
Its exact interval width tends to zero. The support intersection bounds all widths
by 2H. Boundary sets of the initial partition also have measure zero. Dominated
convergence now gives convergence of the integrated width. Vanishing outward
padding preserves the argument. It does not justify removing the actual fixed-
precision remainder from a finite calculation.
There are r2q subboxes per action and P retained actions. The direct binary64
precomputation enumerates O(n4) rectangles and scans at most n2 entries each. A
stored rectangle extremum then uses its four indices. For m = r2q boxes, the inde-
pendent algorithm spends O(m log m) work grouping codes and at most O(mn2)
work enumerating their actor indices. Finally, keeping only one alternative’s in-

Q.E.D.
These are counts for the actual two-date procedure. They are not a reduction of

for process peak memory. The completed R83 recovery records its verification
clock and peak resident memory separately from the interrupted R82 phase clocks.
Development pilots informed the dyadic resolution before the source freeze; the
computation is described as deterministic verification rather than a prospectively
selected new economic experiment.
DR.3. A classwide adoption decision on the original event
Let the signed optimizer-sublevel interval for Jπj −Jπk be [L,U] after applying
(A.114). If deployment of class k rather than class j has an additional total charge τ,
the net advantage of k belongs to [L −τ,U −τ] for every allowed pair of readouts
on the same original event. Thus τ < L supports k uniformly and τ > U supports
the opposite decision uniformly. The intermediate region remains unresolved. This
statement prices construction, verification and installation only when their con-
version into economic cost units is explicitly supplied. A measured second of
verification is not itself such a price.
The extension uses a deterministic outer set of possible acquired actions. It permits
the qualification tolerance or the comparison to be selected after observing the
original simultaneous cost event, provided the original attained controllers and
event are not changed and the stated deterministic enclosures hold. There is no new
probability expenditure over an uncountable set of readouts. Conversely, a newly
fitted hidden-feature model, a changed terminal actor, altered transition law or new
statistical estimand is not covered merely because its displayed objective resembles
the one here.

APPENDIX DS: EXACT INVERSION, BOUNDARY CHECKS AND
SOURCE-QUALIFIED RECOVERY
DS.1. A finite algorithm for the entire tolerance interval
For one construction, let P be the number of integrated nonreference actions and
N the number of acquisition cells. Sort the action events by DCb −U. Events with
nonpositive threshold are active at zero. Maintain the lowest lower endpoint and
highest upper endpoint on each cell, initially including the exact reference interval
[0,0]. When an event is activated, update those two extrema and their probability-
weighted sums. Equal thresholds are processed together. The resulting records
contain every knot, the two class endpoints, the number of admitted alternatives,
and the open or closed status of the stratum’s right endpoint.
PROPOSITION A.82—Exact finite inversion: Suppose the switch bounds, attained
objectives, cell masses and integrated endpoints are rational. The complete class band is

computed with O(P log P + N) comparisons and arithmetic operations after integration,
using O(P + N) storage. Let Kj, Kk denote the numbers of tolerance strata for two con-
structions. For a fixed replacement charge or equivalence margin, the sufficient region in
Theorem A.51 can be represented by at most Kj horizontal strips and found using at most
Kj + Kk endpoint-predicate evaluations. The same bound applies to a certified ordering in
the opposite direction.
PROOF: Sorting costs O(P log P) comparisons. Each event changes at most two
cell extrema and two weighted sums; reference initialization takes O(N) work.
Storing events, cells and resulting strata uses the stated memory. These counts
exclude the already paid action integration, and rational bit complexity depends on
the input denominators.
Order both stratum lists from smaller to larger tolerance. Start at the largest
second-coordinate stratum. For the current first-coordinate stratum, decrease the
second index until the desired endpoint test holds or the index is exhausted. Record
the resulting maximal admissible second-coordinate prefix. Move to the next first-
coordinate stratum and continue from the same second index. Monotonicity implies
that this index never needs to increase. Each successful test advances the first
coordinate, and each failed test decreases the second coordinate. There are at most
Kj + Kk tests. Each recorded strip has the first stratum’s exact endpoint convention
and the upper boundary convention of its last admitted second stratum. Exhaustion
leaves no later feasible strip. Thus the algorithm returns precisely the largest region
certified by these fixed endpoint tests, not merely an inner grid of isolated tolerance
points.
Q.E.D.
The implementation also enumerates the finite product grid independently and
checks every returned and excluded stratum pair. Separately, it rebuilds the possible-
action set directly from the original switch predicates at every knot, every adjacent-
stratum midpoint and the final endpoint. This check does not reuse the incremental
cell-extremum update. It includes negative and repeated switch thresholds, a switch
at the maximum allowed tolerance, and strict sign or equivalence tests at equality.
An economic margin and an objective excess are not interchangeable numbers.
The plotted or tabulated tolerance region is an implication from one to the other

DS.2. Finite numerical and statistical domains
The integrated catalogue is complete up to ej = 1/4096. Actions whose switch
lower bound exceeds Uj + ej cannot be selected within that objective sublevel and
require no economic integration for this result. The calculation does not extrapolate
the band beyond ej. Each class has its original labels, feature map, coefficient box,
acquisition grid, robust action menu and fixed terminal actor. Changing any of these
objects requires new qualification and, where relevant, a new integration account.
There is no new empirical-Bernstein event in this inversion. The original nine-
controller simultaneous event supplies the attained marginal and paired costs.
The actionwise bounds extend it deterministically to all admissible readouts and
tolerances. A data-selected comparison or stopping tolerance is covered because
the event already implies every stated comparison. An unlisted controller or an
additional statistical estimand does not acquire coverage merely by receiving a
similar display name.
For a common tolerance the sufficient region is an initial interval, possibly empty
or the entire declared domain. When a switch destroys the endpoint test, its exact
knot is the supremum and is excluded. Decimal summaries must therefore not be
used as executable stopping thresholds. The deposited rational boundaries and
their inclusion flags are authoritative. A deployment fee is handled by comparing
the lower gain endpoint with the supplied fee, not by converting a measured second
into a monetary amount without a declared exchange rate.

whether those proposals are admissible.

DU.4. Why both refinements matter
For three action scores 0,−1,−2, the second action defeats the reference score
zero but cannot win the full menu. A reference-only barrier can therefore remain
inconclusive even though the complete winner event is empty. This is a distinction
about the implemented argmin, not a change in the economic action set.
For the shared-coefficient restriction, take θ ∈[−1,1] and two cells. An adverse
action in the first cell requires θ ≥1; one in the second requires θ ≤−1. Both
events are separately feasible but their intersection is empty. If each adverse action
contributes 1/2 to aggregate cost, independent cell bounds allow a cost increase
of one. The compatible bound is 1/2, and it is attained by one endpoint of the
parameter interval. This supplies a strict example for the improvement claimed by
the theorem.
Pair restrictions need not characterize every feasible policy. With three unit-
weight alternatives and all three pair conflicts, an assignment relaxation permits
mass 1/2 on each alternative, even though a zero–one assignment can select at most
one. The corresponding fractional support can therefore be larger than the true
worst cost. More generally, pairwise intersection does not imply joint intersection

DU.5. Work, storage and continuation scope
Let P be the number of admitted alternatives, K the number of declared joint
events, m the maximum menu size, d the readout dimension, N the number of cells,
and E the number of retained pair cuts at a tolerance. A singleton event adds at most
m −1 rows and a pair event at most 2(m −1) rows to the same fixed qualification
problem. The experiment executes exactly P + K qualification problems. It does
not claim a dimension-independent bound on an LP solver’s arithmetic or bit
complexity.
Once multipliers have been obtained, checking a qualification certificate takes
a number of rational operations linear in its feature, derivative and event coeffi-
cients. Checking one assignment dual takes O(P + N + E) rational operations and
storage linear in its retained variables, cells and cuts. Constructing and solving
the assignment LP is separate work. The executed pair budget limits qualification
work without assuming that unchecked intersections are feasible or infeasible. Pre-
viously purchased conditional integration remains an explicit prerequisite, not free
computation.
The identity transferring conditional contrasts to aggregate policy cost holds
because the policies share the stated future controller and only their first acquired
action varies. A longer horizon can use the same identity when its entire fixed-
continuation conditional cost is enclosed. Jointly refitting that future controller
changes the estimand and requires another qualification argument. The results
therefore do not claim that the present pair graph certifies arbitrary changes at
every date or regenerates the large vector-control descendant tree.

Equivalence requires the exact rational interval to be strictly inside the predeclared margin. It is
distinct from a signed ranking; both can hold for a small nonzero cost difference. The displayed six-
decimal endpoints are descriptive and do not decide a boundary test. Each interval is displayed on
two lines, with its lower endpoint above its upper endpoint; no endpoint digit or catalogue row
is omitted.
Every alternative previously admitted up to 2−12 is included in the
singleton roster. The fixed pair-selection rule, including its deterministic cost-based
ordering and tie handling, is part of the source lock. Its execution contributes no
additional independent cost row or fit. The 24 model–tolerance records and 36 class
comparisons use the already covered original-law cost family. Source, output and
execution-clock hashes are retained with the exact multipliers, all 104 infeasibility
certificates, and all 16,548 independently checked assignment inequalities.

The fixed evaluation program reconstructs the R85 streams from the protocol and

DW.1. Complete interval family and width components

width = endpoint enclosure
+ sampling variance allowance

DW.2. Selected-service price and fee breakpoints
Every comparison is selected minus comparator. If the upper cost endpoint is u,
then the guaranteed extra-fee ceiling at zero resource price is −λu. With resource
prices it becomes −λu −p · (wbj −wk). Negative ceilings are retained: they do not
support a positive fee based solely on policy quality. A declared normalized loss
margin does not calibrate λ or a monetary fee.

DW.3. Diagnostics and independently checked kernels
The new exact fixtures compare path enumeration with forward occupation re-
cursion, test the candidate-occupation counterexample, retain ties, reject impossible
shared-parameter assignments, and exhibit a fractional outer bound that is valid but
unattained. Separate tests check the ReLU/min-plus identity, label-noise enclosure,
persistent-exploration recursion, sufficient screen closure, correct lower-versus-
upper work comparison, dated allocation, and price-region boundaries.
The frozen evaluation records zero new fits. Predictor warning rates, fallback
frequencies and zero-progress query probes are not identified by that fact. Earlier
fitting warnings and their affected services remain in the inherited experiment
records. The R70 audit covers 188 service processes and records its prediction-
replay differences; it is not a 336-service manifest. The source-specific diagnostic
index records these distinctions instead of assigning unsupported aggregate counts
to the current evaluation.

The large inherited vector descendant tree, a derivative branch-and-bound com-

the original algorithms, economic applications or full-horizon theorems from the
manuscript.
DW.4. Publication identity
Current document hashes, source hashes, test counts, exact replay status and
clean reconstruction status are recorded under the current revision’s audit directory.
A publication gate rejects absent current PDFs, bibliographies or source-matched
checks. Visual inspection is a separately signed-off observation against actual PDF
hashes; neither a compiler exit code nor an inherited release record is such an
observation. The full preservation edition retains every preceding active substantive
section. Its actual page count is reported rather than concealed by reducing type
size or deleting mathematical content.

experiment has 256 training states, 128 calibration states and 384 evaluation states.
Five services, three repetitions and a second architecture do not multiply these
numbers. The two fitting attempts belong to that original experiment; no new fitting
or independent economic observation is introduced by this reconstruction.

APPENDIX DZ: CURRENT-SOURCE REPRODUCTION AND RETAINED SCOPE
The current reproduction command requires the ordinary article, technical sup-
plement, numerical appendix and response sources, rather than substituting an
older compiled article. It checks the preserved active input list, reconstructs the re-
quired tables, executes the selected mathematical and numerical checks, and records
their exact source and output identities. Each executed check has its own exit sta-
tus and log. A clean typesetting reconstruction removes inherited auxiliary and
bibliography outputs. The final release gate additionally requires a rendered-page
inspection record tied to the actual four PDF hashes.
A compiled candidate, a passed arithmetic test and a visually inspected package
are distinct delivery states. The current manifest determines which states have
actually been attained. The full matched large-vector comparator study, measured
energy and application-specific monetary calibration remain separate evidence
obligations; they are not inferred from the new transport theorem or a successful
build. The original diffusion, recursive-preference, temporal-self and game results
remain in their existing active sections and retained companions under their original
hypotheses.

APPENDIX EB: INDEPENDENT DIAGNOSTICS FOR CENTERED RISK
QUALIFICATION
This section reports deterministic diagnostics of Section 4. They use finite rational
models with three states, two feasible actions and original nested average value at
risk. They are not additional investment observations, new fitting attempts, or a
rerun of the inherited largest-vector problem. The production calculation uses the
vertices of a capped probability simplex. The independent evaluator minimizes the
scalar threshold representation of average value at risk and performs a separately
coded original-value recursion. It does not import the centered-risk implementation.
The declared horizons are 2,3,4,8,16,32,64, risk levels are 0,1/2,3/4, and the
four shared continuation parameters are −1,0,1,2. At date t, state s ∈{0,1,2} and
action a ∈{0,1}, transition weights are
(1 + (t + s + a) mod 3,
1 + (2s + a) mod 4,
1 + (t + 2a) mod 3),
normalized by their sum. Costs are ((s + 2a + t) mod 5 −2)/7 + a/5, the discount
is 3/4, and the terminal vector is (0,1/3,−1/4). These fully specified diagnostic
primitives avoid a hidden change in objective between implementations. They are
separate from the paper’s economic calibration.
A single parameter determines the stored circuit throughout a configuration:

The implemented policy is greedy for this circuit under the original one-step eval-

prescribed circuits. Residual intervals use radii 0,1/64,1/8 times (1 + s)/3; termi-
nal intervals use the same statewise radius. The exact configuration records retain
the complete input, every centered residual and risk penalty, lower and upper
potentials, a feasible maximizing risk occupation, and all strict kernel-exclusion
certificates. Unpruned potential bounds are computed before any exclusion, pre-
venting circular error boxes.

APPENDIX EC: CONTINUOUS-RISK EVIDENCE, UNCERTAINTY, AND
PRESERVATION
This section records the continuous investment execution separately from the
retained finite-risk catalogue and the earlier expected-cost experiments. All new
scientific calculations use the unchanged R94 protocol and numerical source. The
R95 additions supply the primitive proofs, the integrated manuscript, the complete
diagnostic summary and source-bound validation of the resulting evidence.
EC.1. Complete comparisons and screened work
The full retained files contain 2,048 rows for each of four arms at each risk level,
for 16,384 arm-state records and 4,096 independent initial-state observations. Every
first action, gap, original-optimum bound, cost enclosure and failed-target count
is retained. There are six fitting attempts, all in preparation. Calibration uses 128
separate states per risk level. Supplementary terminal calculations at dimensions
four and eight use 16 prespecified states each and have no primary inferential
weight. They are not a replication of the earlier vector-control experiment.
The empirical-Bernstein intervals have one family confidence level of 95% for
twelve prespecified contrasts. Their numerical endpoints and sampling radii are
computed from every row, using a proved support rather than observed extrema.
Conservative Hoeffding intervals are retained as well; a favorable rule is not selected
after evaluation. The fixed sample size, margin and confidence rule are those in the
pre-evaluation protocol.
Numerical components.
The original innovation is uniform on [−1/32,1/32]. The
one-date original terminal risk is integrated analytically and enclosed outwards.

The unit is an independent initial state under the declared dyadic uniform distribution. There are
twelve fixed comparisons in one family. Equivalence uses the prespecified margin 1/16 in normalized
cost units. Every interval includes zero: none identifies strict superiority. The calibration selector is

First-date integration uses full-bin bounds. A half-bin contributes the explicit con-
tinuation allowance 15/(32n); a complete terminal controller contributes at most
2−20 before first-date discounting. State observation and terminal optimization are
bounded together by 2−21 + 302−40 < 2−20. Arithmetic rounding is propagated
through the interval operations rather than replaced by an unverified final decimal
tolerance. These allowances overlap with conservative bin bounds in the code and
must not be added again to the final cost interval. State covers qualify residuals;
they do not change the transition law. There is no numerical entropic evaluation in
this experiment.

EC.3. Source, execution and release boundaries
The controlling advisory report is the R92 review deposited on 13 October 2026.
Its reviewed manuscript is the complete R92 article. The R94 development branch is
a descendant of that manuscript; its paper entry point had not yet incorporated its
new continuous-risk implementation. R95 retains the original title and author, adds
the continuous primitive proof and executed comparison, and relocates fifteen com-
plete historical main-text sections to this appendix. Each moved file is byte-identical
to the R92 source. The only inherited scientific-section prose amendment clarifies
that the earlier experiments use expectation, while the new explicitly specified ex-
periment uses nested AVaR. No original mathematical claim or adverse observation
is removed.
The cloud R94 attempt stopped before scientific execution when creation of its
source branch was rejected. The available source-and-evidence artifact therefore
contains sources but no completed primary run. R95 executed those sources locally.

Preservation.
The preceding investment, risk, screening, approximation, and
vector-control studies retain their original data and assumptions. The original
R96 manuscript sources remain under the pinned historical revision, and the cur-
rent revision retains unmodified scientific section files. The current article uses a
workload-corrected copy of the precision section; the uncorrected historical file is
not overwritten. Primitive investment accuracy, horizon allocation, and intervening
proof sections are reproduced below as complete sections, rather than removed to
shorten the active article.
Audit interpretation.
A binary64 independent proposal replay checks an im-
plementation at the declared action-quantization tolerance; it is not an exact-real
decision proof. Exact rational arithmetic checks the statistical contrasts and selected
difficult original-law endpoint cases. The original random 64-case audit and the new
deterministic extremal audit have different selection rules. Neither is mislabeled
as a rational reconstruction of every endpoint, independent authorship, or a fully
independent numerical-optimization stack. The source and discrepancy receipts
allow each claim to be inspected at its actual scope.
APPENDIX EF: ORIGINAL-OPTIMUM ACCURACY IN THE INVESTMENT ECONOMY
The exact witness theorem answers an implementation question conditional on
a continuation. An economist also needs to know how close the complete imple-
mented policy is to the original optimum. We now establish that connection in the
investment economy itself. The argument exploits a property not used by the earlier
cell-range calculation: despite the bilinear transition, the Bellman objective remains
jointly convex. This permits a second-order interpolation account and transfers
verified nodal decisions to an implementable policy over the entire state domain. It
does not assume that a fitted neural continuation is convex.

the fixed shared capacity 1/8. The complete dynamic extension below uses the
original state-dependent capacity c(x), with the retained exposure columns, action-
cost interaction and second shock. Its nesting claim concerns the original scalar

EF.4. Arithmetic, work, and scope
The native interpolation kernel forms nonnegative tensor weights and a weighted
sum of at most 2d stored binary64 endpoints. It is compiled without reassociation or
floating-point contraction. For K = (3d + 4)2d + 32, an explicit conservative absolute
allowance is
η =
K2−53
1 −K2−53 max
v
|zv| + K2−1022.
The final term conservatively covers underflow. Input coordinates, affine indexing,
finite endpoints and the binary64 format are checked. Roundoff expansion and the
ordinary interval cost arithmetic remain separate from the analytic approximation
bounds. Exact rational fixtures compare the native sum with its mathematical tensor
interpolant.
With N = (n + 1)d vertices, KA = A + 1 scalar actions or KA = (A + 1)(A +
2)/2 two-control actions, the reference calculation uses O(TNKAqs2dd) elementary
work under the explicit tensor implementation. Stored reference values use O(TN)
words and a policy uses O(TNm) words. Streaming batches avoid a state-pair
table. Proposal fitting, exact rational witness work, actor transfer, serialization,
independent cost inference and compilation are additional costs, not absorbed into
this bound. The analytic errors are second order in state, action and innovation
resolution; the state-count and tensor-evaluation factors still depend exponentially
on dimension. The result supplies a matched original-optimum comparison without
asserting that these costs have disappeared.

EG.1. Operation vectors, arithmetic and reliability
We retain the resource vector
(Nprimitive, Ndescendant, Ninterval, Nrational, Nnetwork, Bread, Bwrite, Mpeak).
Counts are reported before scalar prices are applied. Rational operations addition-
ally record operand bit lengths; an arithmetic-operation count is not a bit-complexity
bound. Multiplication and division costs at those lengths enter a bit-cost account.
Loading, validation, serialization and shutdown belong to complete process time.
Peak memory is a capacity requirement, not an additive flow cost unless its duration
or rental convention is specified.
A fitting warning, invalid proposal, zero-progress probe, successful screen, pro-
tected fallback and terminal service status are different events. In particular, zero
new fits cannot estimate fitting reliability, and a successful fallback cannot be
counted as a successful prediction. The retained 336-service recursive catalogue
and the nine-controller attained-cost experiment have different units of observation.

APPENDIX EI: PROOFS OF THE OPERATIONAL AND NEW RESULTS
EI.1. Proof of the result A.75
PROOF: Strong convexity gives f ((1 −s)l + su) ≤(1 −s) f (l) + s f (u) −µs(1 −
s)(u −l)2/2. Replacing the endpoint values by their upper bounds proves (A.165).
Subtraction of a valid lower bound proves (A.166). A failed screen adds no endpoint
to the partition and alters no lower bound. Subsequent protected refinement is
therefore covered by the earlier termination proof. A successful screen supplies
exactly the local accuracy premise used in the acquired-policy recursion. Finally, C
is a convex quadratic in a, proving the sublevel-set assertion.
Q.E.D.
EI.2. Proof of the result A.76
PROOF: A successful screen returns without an endpoint query. A failed screen
invokes a procedure bounded by K(z), and its margin loss equals one. This proves
(A.169). For each fixed predictor the variable K(z)ℓτ(z, θ) lies in [0, Kmax]. The
bounded-sum inequality of Hoeffding (1963) and a union bound over the con-
ditionally fixed family give (A.170).
Q.E.D.

APPENDIX EJ: RETAINED INTERVENING TRAINING RESULTS
EJ.1. Proof of Proposition A.66
PROOF: A successful screen incurs no recovery queries. On a failed screen the
clipped loss equals one, and recovery work is at most WK. The pointwise bound
therefore holds for the bounded variable WKℓτ. The bounded-sum inequality and a
union bound give the claim. None of the separately named service costs is included
in the definition of recovery work.
Q.E.D.
EJ.2. Proof of Proposition A.67
PROOF:
The lower cover still covers the entire feasible set, so its unchanged
lower bound remains valid. Each additional upper endpoint bounds the true cost of
its own feasible action, hence is an upper bound for the infimum. Their minimum
preserves this property. The returned action’s true cost is no greater than its own
upper endpoint, proving the regret claim.
Q.E.D.

EK.4. Capacity rounding and the fill bound
PROOF OF PROPOSITION A.71:
Let cq(x) = q⌊c(x)/q⌋. If an already lattice-
aligned ay has total mass no greater than cq(x), it is unchanged. Otherwise pro-
portional reduction removes total mass ∑i(ay)i −cq(x), and downward rounding
removes less than mq more. Since cq(x) > c(x) −q and ay ∈A(y), the total displace-

Before the favorable zero truncation of the lower bound, the expanded width is
no greater than
γδ + (LV + LQ + κLA)D + LA(m + 1)q + ξ.
It is at most δ for D ≤ρ∗. Because all records are checked and retained, two centers
at which fresh fills are purchased must consequently be more than ρ∗apart in ℓ1.
Partition each coordinate of the unit cube into n = ⌈d/ρ∗⌉equal intervals, with a
fixed boundary convention. The diameter of each resulting box is at most d/n ≤ρ∗.
It can contain at most one fresh center. Thus Mr ≤nd ≤(1 + d/ρ∗)d. Each fill is paid
once, whereas every query incurs its actual lookup, verification and record handling.

separation argument applies only within a period in which the required earlier
records remain available; lost coverage must be repurchased and charged. Q.E.D.

the positive shortage is at most 1/2, and a ≤1/4. Substitution into the nonnegative
cost terms gives c ≤103/64 and g ≤37/16. Discounting gives (A.136); conditional

elementary lower endpoint is moved to the adjacent lower representable number
and each upper endpoint to the adjacent upper number. For integer-directed opera-
tions, multiplication on the 2−48 grid uses the floor of the smallest endpoint product
divided by 248 and the ceiling of the largest. Division by a positive integer uses the
corresponding integer floor and ceiling. Addition and negation are exact on this
grid. Squaring includes zero when its argument interval straddles zero, and the
positive-part map is monotone. These rules enclose the result of each elementary
operation.
Induction through either polynomial formula therefore encloses the cost and
transition of every point in the input box. At an acquisition step, each possible
true state belongs to one of the enumerated intersected cells, so its deployed action
lies between the enumerated extrema. A second induction through the two dates
proves the full-bin cost enclosure. Conditional final integration is valid by the exact
identity already proved. The state and cost intersections use established primitive
supports. Taking the hull of two valid intervals is conservative even when one
is wider. Neither interval intersection with a sampled value nor agreement at a
midpoint is used to establish this full-bin claim.
In the statistical implementation, sample sums and sums of squares are integers.
Their rational combination gives the unbiased variance exactly. For a rational v ≥0,
the least k satisfying k2 ≥2120v gives the upward square root k/260. Each radius
enlargement is less than 2−60, except that it is zero for an exactly represented root.
The recorded width decomposition uses these enlarged roots and is an exact rational

When the transitions and advantages are exact on a finite state space, δt = ωt = 0.
Each fixed pattern has a unique occupation sequence; the convex mixture of their
costs has the same minimum and maximum as this finite set. A retained qualification
witness therefore attains each extremal policy value. More generally the quantitative
inequalities prove the stated convergence whenever E tends to zero uniformly. This
is not a claim that arbitrary partitions, discontinuous deterministic transitions or
incomplete pattern searches satisfy that condition.
EN.3. Strict improvement in the shared-sign example
Let θ = 1 select the right-hand initial action and the free action at the right-hand
successor. Let θ = −1 select the left-hand initial action and the costly action at the
right-hand successor. All other costs are zero. Both complete policies cost zero. In
the conflict relaxation, set the right-hand initial assignment and occupation to 1/2,
and the right-hand costly assignment and occupation also to 1/2. Put the remaining
initial mass on the left-hand action; choose the free action in the left-hand successor.
The forbidden pair’s assignments sum to one, so its conflict inequality holds. Its
cost is 1/2. Conversely that cost cannot exceed either member of the forbidden pair,
whose assignments sum to one, and thus is at most 1/2. Pattern disaggregation
has only the two zero-cost occupation sequences and gives upper bound zero. The
numerical test computes the three bounds by independent path enumeration and
linear programming.

EP.3. State-independent shifts and singular laws
Replace ft by ft + kt and bQt by bQt + βtkt+1. Since both kernels have total mass
one, the arithmetic discrepancy, transport modulus and greedy gap are unchanged.
The approximate Bellman residual is shifted by βtkt+1 −kt. Its certified lower and
upper endpoints shift by that same amount, so their difference is unchanged. The
terminal enclosure endpoints both decrease by kT. Every term of Rθ is consequently
invariant. Using absolute levels of the continuation in place of its oscillation would
forfeit this property.
If bPt is the law of qt(Y) when Y has law Pt, the joint law of (Y, qt(Y)) is a coupling.
Its expected distance is at most ht. Thus W1(Pt, bPt) ≤ht. Substitution into 2 ∑t Btbt
gives (A.129). In particular, δh and δ0 have transport distance h but total-variation
distance supA |δh(A) −δ0(A)| = 1 when h > 0. Mutual singularity therefore does
not obstruct this continuation-based calculation. The conclusion concerns the trans-
port contribution only; a nonvanishing residual span or greedy error still has to be
paid.

EP.5. Resource allocation and the other economic objectives
With ηt ≥ut −ℓt + γt, the sufficient budget (A.130) is obtained by rearrang-
ing the nonnegative terms in Rθ. After subtracting fixed terminal and arithmetic
contributions, it is a linear budget in the residual and transport allowances. On
positive-weight coordinates, any resource upper model satisfying Theorem A.41
has that theorem’s convexity, attainment, dyadic-rounding and dual-certificate
properties. This is a direct application with additional accuracy coordinates, not a
newly asserted lower bound on all numerical methods. Caps and certificates for the
moduli are part of the input. Optimizing a modulus jointly requires retaining its
parameter dependence in the resource and error constraints.
For a cash-invariant monotone one-step risk operator with discount βt, a certified
numerical discrepancy bt gives the same two residual inequalities and the same
constant-shift induction. Neither the coupling proof for linear expectation nor cash
invariance alone supplies that numerical discrepancy for a nonlinear risk functional.
For a general Lipschitz aggregator, the separate absolute-error induction in Proposi-
tion A.27 supplies the valid replacement. Applying an original-optimum bound to
each fixed-opponent best-response problem gives the stated unilateral incentive ac-
count; it does not prove existence of a game equilibrium. These arguments preserve
the distinct hypotheses of the original applications.
EP.6. Diagnostic with a falsely free transition approximation
In the one-date example, both numerical action values are constants: zero for
action 0 and h/2 for action 1. Hence bT f1 −f0 = 0, the numerical greedy gap is
zero, and the terminal enclosure is exact. The true values of the two actions are h
and h/2, respectively. The numerical greedy policy therefore has regret h/2. The
stored terminal function has modulus one and the largest transport discrepancy is
h, so Theorem A.54 gives 2h. The omitted-charge expression is zero and is invalid.
